title: Solid Single Player RPG
text:
Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning is the first offering from 38 Studios, the game development company founded a few years ago by former Major League pitcher Curt Schilling. The game's world and lore has had substantial creative input from the best-selling fantasy author R.A. Salvatore, and has also had substantial input from several well-known game designers and developers at Big Huge Games, a company that 38 acquired from THQ a few years ago. In a nutshell, the game has a good deal of quality development power behind it, and it shows.

38 Studios is mostly focused on MMORPG development, and has a project already in the works. In some ways, this is reflected in this game, because the game often plays like a single player MMORPG. This has good and bad aspects, and may not appeal to all gamers, for the reasons I describe below.

First, graphically the game feels like World of Warcraft. That is -- the graphics are more of the cartoon/stylized variety than the more realistic kind found in single player games like The Witcher 2 or Skyrim. The color scheme of the world also tends toward bright, vivid colors in a way that reminds one of WoW's artistic approach. As a result, less of an emphasis is placed on extremely high-resolution textures, and more on overall feel and style. It's inevitable that this will turn off some single-player game fans, who prefer games like Skyrim with realistic, high-resolution graphics.

Second, the progression in the game is not as linear as something like Mass Effect, but instead features zone progression -- as in, you start in one area/zone, complete the quests in that zone, and then are moved on to the next zone, where there is another pack of quests. The NPC enemies/monsters in these zones do not scale, unlike a game like Skyrim, so as your character levels, the open-world monsters will become trivial in earlier zones. In that sense, although it is more of an open world game than something like Mass Effect or Dragon Age: Origins, in that you are actually moving around in the open world rather than porting between snippets of it, it nevertheless plays more like an MMO in this respect than a game like Skyrim. I do not see this as a drawback, but some players may.

Beyond these, the game plays like a good, polished single player RPG. It does feel like a console game at times, even when playing on the PC, due to the control scheme, the camera angles, and the way the character moves and feels -- this is becoming fairly common in computer RPGs these days, and similar kinds of issues were present in Skyrim's menus system as well.

Combat is probably the highlight of the game, and in this aspect it does not play like an MMORPG at all, or like a traditional RPG (as the first Dragon Age did) but like an action RPG. The combat is fast-paced and fluid, the character is responsive, and the ways and means are quite varied. The player can choose a melee warrior setup, a rogue/stealth setup or a mage type setup, or any combination of the above, in going about combat. The game makes it very easy to change one's approach (for a smallish in-game currency fee) to suit a different kind of combat style, and the game offers a substantial variety of weapons and skills that all can be used to alter one's approach to combat and how one essentially plays the game. One point worthy of mention is that the game's default difficulty setting is probably too easy for advanced gamers, and the hard setting probably feels like a normal mode to hardcore gamers -- at some point perhaps a true nightmare mode will be released for hardcore gamers.

The story is well-done, as one would expect with the input of someone like Salvatore, and functions as a good introduction to this new setting and world. The game accomplishes this credibly and well from the very beginning, with an interesting, fully-blown world and lore revealed gradually to the player. The larger implications of the story are also fairly interesting, particularly once one advances along the quest lines a bit further. The voice over dialogue scenes are not going to be confused with a BioWare game, but at the same time the overall game design for Amalur is much more open world than is the case for a BioWare game, and the voice over dialogue is present but much less of a focus. The use of lorestones and other means to tell the story is an interesting and enjoyable approach, in my opinion.

In all, this is a very good effort as the first release from 38 Studios. It's polished, deep, long and fun to play. Hopefully we will see more of this interesting world and setting in future games from 38 -- maybe even in the MMORPG they are currently developing.

title: You did it again Enix
text:
What a game- let me tell you. There are some great parts from the original one they included; unique bosses, awesome new weapons, a great storyline. Though were there are some great parts there must be bad.

Kingdom Hearts II was a blast, I loved battling enemy after enemy, the tiny stars that flash up when you attack something with your keyblade reassured me of that. Let me tell you though the beginning started off very slow and confusing. Let me tell you now if you haven't beaten Kingdom Hearts 1 you'll probably be scratching your head the whole game.

You first start off as Roxas, a boy who is suddenly plunged into the Kingdom Hearts storyline. Similar to Kingdom Heart's first part of the game, I can honestly say(and I'm sure many would agree with me) that is was extremely boring and slow. Agh chore after chore, job after job. I hated collecting all that money, preforming stupid tricks on some skateboard that you couldn't skip! The only thing that really struck my attention in that part were the dreams Roxas had- It got me interested in the mysterious, devolping storyline yet to come. Well you can't blame Enix I suppose, I guess they were only trying to build up to the juicy parts.

Oh yes the juicy parts, chopping and slicing every enemy I see with my trusty keyblade- classic Kingdom Hearts. The "ultima" keyblade has returned, just as hard to make, just as powerful, and just as awesome looking. Saving world after world, it was very entertaining how different and unique each world was.

Although I was not use to the whole new gummi ship system, I grew to like it and now I realize it was a ton better than the first one. The trips where you battle hoards of flying enemies might be a little slow and easy at first, but trust me it really starts heating up when you get to the harder worlds. They now have a new boss system, where a boss might randomly attack you in battle. These guys are toughies if you don't have the right equipment, and I think Enix really tried to encourage that. Not only that, you can now travel to the same trips but on a different difficulty level. Rewards for completion include rare gummi peices. Perfect Enix, perfect.

One of my favorite parts were the drive powers. The game so totally needed this. Sora now has the power to weild TWO keyblades at once. That's right... you heard me, two! There are four drive powers that you can activate with a new drive bar similar the magic bar. Already the first power given to you early in the game allows Sora to weild two keyblades. I won't go over the next two, but the last one is a whopper! The final form, as Enix named it is just awesome. Sora's clothes turn totally silver and black, two keyblades hover(that's right hover!) around his hands, he hovers around in midair, and to top it all off when you attack you do insane damage, along with special moves you couldn't do with regular attacks. I would have to say this was one of the most enjoyable parts of this wonderful game.

I'm sorry to say though that the game was really quite easy. Now if I recall correctly one of the fairy people in the beginning mentioned something like "This adventure is going to be twice as difficult!". Man I was all prepared for this great journey, but at the end when I beat it I felt a sence of dispair. I felt as if I had just pressed the "x" button over and over, as a previous customer mentioned. Bosses that use to take quite a long time to kill can now be killed in less than a minute, and you don't even have to be a high combat level. When I defeated bosses in the first one, I felt a sence of accomplishment, but now I don't when the bosses kneel before me in KH2.

Overall- I like to say congratulations Square Enix for once again creating a great game.

This game took less than a few hours to beat and added very little to the depth of the walking dead storyline.

Traveling from point A to B requires using a vehicle that gives 3 options for travel. The safest using the most gas and the most dangerous using the least gas but more likely to break down or run into road blocks. Which seems like a neat concept but gets more tedious than anything else.

They use maybe a dozen different models for zombies, so they all look pretty much the same after about the first 30 minutes in game. Also there is no method for zombie respawn, you kill a dozen down a street and go clear something else just to find zombies in exactly the same place you killed them before just respawned. Which makes it tedious to explore cause your likely to kill the same zombies over and over again just running around.

I was really disappointed with this game, I was hoping for a much richer story with better kill animations and overall better graphics. Also considering they released it for 50 dollars originally there is little replay value overall for the money spent

This feels like progress, and by that I mean two steps forward and one step back. The mouse itself is very light weight and looks and feels like it was built from a large eggshell. It has room for either a AA or AAA battery, which is something I hadn't seen before. Choosing your battery size and chemistry should be a simple hack for adjusting the weight, since the mouse itself weighs nearly nothing.

I'm assuming this rough texture and white color combination are going to lead to some unattractive stains over time, but I've got little proof of such as yet.

The ergonomics are nice, but suited for a smaller hand. I've got much smaller mice that feel more natural in a large hand, but it' not bad if you don't mind a couple fingers dragging on the table. The side buttons are especially well placed. Harder than most to hit accidentally, but still very accessible. Tactile feedback is good. The sensitivity adjustment is easy and has more stops than I'm used to, which is nice.

I love the choice of bluetooth or dongle, which is stored within. There's an easy to use three way switch on the underside.

Overall, it doesn't look or feel like a luxury mouse to me, but it's well designed and put together, which is more than I can say for most.

title: I know I'm in the minority, but this game is bad.
text:
I had MVC3 and traded it in and waited for UMVC3 and I completely wasted my time and money. Hard core fighting gamers will probably love this game, but I consider myself a casual to moderate fighting gamer. Here's the pros and cons:

Pros:
-Graphics are pretty cool and stylistic
-Characters are varied
-Marvel superheroes are always cool!

Cons:
-Online mode is supposed to match you up with people your own skill, however I'm noticing many "beginners" and "rookies" are kicking my butt. Then I realized that they aren't really rookies, but people either resesting their stats or creating separate accounts and starting over to easily beat people. That's why everyone I sometimes face user names like "taj134dod"
-The endings are super lame and a huge disappointment.
-Galactus seems a lot harder on this version than in MVC3 on normal.
-Air combos. Worse thing every to happen to fighting games. EVER. Back in the day, Street Fighter II styles, it was about timing and guessing your opponents moves. Now, it's about landing that initial strike (which is good), but then being rewarded for it by doing almost unlimited air combos and taking all of your opponents energy for one initial hit. One opponent used Magento and took almost all my life with one consistant air combo. Go back to a thinking man's fighting game and not fast fingers and NO EXPLOITS. Knocking an opponent into the air and then slamming them back to the ground is fine, but this is just ridiculous.
-You can't quit an online match before it begins. This is especially annoying when you are put up against a way higher ranked player than you and you can't exit.
-Loading and saving. If this game isn't loading it's saving. If it isn't saving, it's loading.

I could go on and on about the game's cons, but unless you're a hard core fighting gamer, than stay clear away from this game. I am trading in my copy for Batman Arkham City or anything else really.

Multiplayer continues from the pick 10 system, with a couple interesting new killstreaks, and mobility options. Different specialists add unique perks that can be helpful, but are mostly frustrating when you get owned by someone else.
Zombies has some great characters, but most of the mechanics remain the same.
Visually, BO3 is better than AW and crushes GHOSTS. The story misses a lot of opportunities for tie-ins with the rest of the series and quality character development. Multiplayer lacks the insane rush nature of AW, feeling slower and more deliberate.

title: Overwatch is a fast-paced first person shooter that brings a sense of sheer delight to the genre not seen since Team Fortress 2
text:
15 million players can't be wrong, right?

Overwatch is a fast-paced first person shooter that brings a sense of sheer delight to the genre not seen since Team Fortress 2. It's not the most competitive of games (bizarre hit boxes and tick rate, balancing issues, these hold it back) but it's easily one of the most fun. Featuring a massive cast of heroes, the learning curve is steep but rewarding. "Training" and "Quick Play" modes help the novice practice and prepare themselves, while offering seasoned players a less-pressuring respite from the "Competitive" mode, where things get a bit more serious. And you'll want to train extensively - each hero is unique and has their own play style and personality, no clones here.

Content-wise, the game can feel a little sparse but Blizzard is clearly hard at work. Just a few months after launch, they've added another hero (for free!) and a fun summer event with special cosmetic unlockables (cosmetics, incidentally, are the only things you can buy outright - no pay to win here) and its own mode of play (which is absolutely a ball.) The game does sorely miss a single-player campaign, especially with the enticing depth of characters and lore. However, this feels like a game that will grow for a long time, so it's not one you'll be quickly bored with.

Graphically, the game ranges from good to adequate, and while it's not exactly stunning in any regard, it generally performs reliably, which I'll alwys prefer. It really shines in sound design, however. Sound cues are clear and really, truly important in this game, adding an extra layer of depth. The music is fun and atmospheric without being intrusive, though not much is memorable besides the main theme.

Five stars do not indicate a perfect game, of course. There are bugs, there are balance issues, there is that really weird tick rate. But Blizzard is listening, communicating, and always updating. This is the most fun I've had with an FPS in ages, and for that, five stars for sure.

title: Console port done right.
text:
Gears of War is a 3rd person shooter developed by Epic Games and published by Microsoft Game Studios. It was first released as an Xbox 360 exclusive, and it went on to become one of the most successful games for the console. It was later released for the PC with some added content and better visuals to support the high end graphics cards.

You play as Marcus Fenix, a former COG soldier who was imprisoned for abandoning his post, and reinstated into command and asked to join the Coalition to fight Locust. The game is quite different from most 3rd person shooters in that, it relies heavily on cover mechanics. You take cover behind various objects during firefights, and stand up to shoot and duck back out of sight.

Even in the casual setting, there is some frustration to be had. Difficulty climbs quite steeply in these sections; I felt there should have been at least one checkpoint during these parts, instead there were none.

The sound track is good, but it could have used more variations. Every time there an action sequence, the same music kicks in throughout the game. Granted that the game itself is not very long, yet, listening to the same tune over and over again tends to get monotonous, and however good it might be. The effects are top notch, weapons pack a punch, especially the top gun and the six-shooter.

Weapons are fun to use. I especially loved the torque bow it reminded me of Rambo. In fact, the whole game feels like a big Hollywood movie. It's very slick and fast paced. The melee combat has some great moments. The chainsaw to the machinegun was a great idea; when you get a chainsaw kill on an enemy, the game takes over and it shows you slicing an enemy into half. As cool as this might be, it could have been implemented better, because sometimes it doesn't work like it should.

The best in the game for me are the visuals. Gears of War uses Unreal 3 engine, and it looks fantastic. I played the game in DirectX 10 mode at 1920x1200 with all settings on maximum on my EVGA GeForce 260GTX, and it looked out of this world. There is something about the art and environment though, while they are beautiful and unique, most of the game the environment is various shades of dirt. This can seem monotonous after a while. This could have used some lush green jungles as seen in Crysis. It would have looked beautiful in Unreal 3 engine.

Technically speaking, there is a nasty savegame bug that causes the savegames to disappear after exit. This happened a few times even after patching it. If you are playing offline, there is a fix, and also a way to backup the save games.

Over all it's a fantastic experience. Gears of War is an excellent port. It has all the qualities of a good port should have and some bad ones too. Controls are very well optimized for the PC. I have no hesitation in recommending this game.

+ Graphics
+ Sound effects
+ Level design
+ Fast paced gameplay
+ Cover system
+ Weapons, especially torque bow

- Savegame bug
- Repetitive soundtrack
- Uneven checkpoints on two occasions

Verdict - Must play

title: Fantastic Reprise of a Classic
text:
Shogun: Total War was the title that marked the beginning of the Total War series of games -- games which feature a combination of strategic/turn-based play on a campaign map and tactical/real-time army combat on a 3D battlefield map. The original Shogun was a fabulous game, and, after years and several other iterations of Total War, including Medieval, Rome, Empire and Napoleon, Creative Assembly have returned to reprise their classic game, and done so fabulously well.

Shogun 2 drips with the atmosphere of medieval Japanese clan warfare and intrigue. The voices, the music, the scenery, and even the diplomacy are all period and region perfect, and give the game an unforgettable atmosphere. The campaign map reprises the clans of the classic game, with Japan divided among numerous warring clans, each headed by a Daimyo/warlord. The player controls one such clan, and must manage his clan's economy, trade routes and income, family relationships, general loyalties and roles, diplomacy with other clans, construction of buildings, military units and naval ships, spying/subterfuge/assasination/religious conversion and, of course, warfare. The basic outlines are, of course similar to those of the other games of the series, but with markedly less "bloat" than we have seen in some of the more recent titles -- units are more streamlined, which makes some aspects of the battles more intuitive.

The game, however, is set at a challenging level. Even advanced Total War players will find the challenging settings to be very challenging indeed. Newcomers to the series may find even the easy setting to be challenging as well. The AI in Shogun 2 is smarter, more adaptive, and more aggressive, at lower difficulty settings, than in previous titles of the series. This added level of challenge gives the game more depth, and keeps the player on his toes, although it can be admittedly frustrating if you have a low frustration tolerance or are more tuned to the difficulty settings of earlier games in the series. However, if you enjoy a bit more of a challenge, you'll find Shogun 2 to be a wonderfully engaging strategy game that will provide interesting play for quite some time.

In all, this is a must for any fan of the Total War series, and probably the best game of the series to date. Any serious strategy game fan should give this game a shot -- you won't be disappointed.

title: Incredible...but the fun and plot are short lived.
text:
I'll admit it, I'm an RPG junky. I've always been drawn to games where you the player gets to make the decisions to influence the outcome of the game. The more decisions, the better!

Fable and Fable II are pretty unique in how they allow the player to interact with the non-player-characters (NPC), and how your decisions impact the appearance of your character.

Basically you're presented with a series of missions, some are honorable like "rescue the slaves" while others are rather evil like "assasinate a good person." As you work your way through these missions, you begin to build a reputation for your good and bad deeds and the townsfolk respond to you appropriately.

You can interact with the town in the same manner. If you knock on someone's door and they do not answer, you have the option of smashing the door in. While you're walking around a shop, you can choose to steal things...it's all up to you.

There is actually ALOT happening in this game. There are several mini-games (jobs) such as blacksmithing, woodcutting, bartending etc. These involve hitting a button on the controller within a certain window of opportunity for the character to complete an action. You will receive gold and unlock achievements by blacksmithing for example.

When interacting with shop keepers, you can actually get lower prices by treating the shop owners in a certain way. If you flirt with them or dance for them, they will usually change their prices. You can also buy shops and earn money or buy homes, redecorate them and rent them out.

Unlike Fable I, you have a dog that follows you around and helps you find treasure chests and dig-spots. I found that most of the treasure was absolute junk. You could easily go through the entire game without needing to dig or discover and open chests.

Many of these actions aren't really necessary to move forward in the gameplay/plot...so it's really a matter of how fast you want to move through the game. Once you've managed to get your hands on a master-level weapon with an augmentation like GHOUL, you won't have too difficult of a time with killing anything...so what use will you have for gold?

The plot had many simularities with Fable I and I actually think it was weaker in many respects. The sole complaint I had with Fable I is that it was too short! Once you finish the storyline, there's very little to do...it makes you almost not want to advance in the game!

Great game, outstanding graphics, cool gameplay, cool features etc. but the developers could have done a much better job in tying everything together in a cohesive manner to make more of these mini-games an actual part of the story/game.

I would recommend you rent this badboy from blockbuster for 10 days. If you've got 10 days to devote to playing it, you'll probably have it finished off in about 7 depending on how long you play each day...you'll save money doing this...trust me.

I love this controller. It's not perfect, it's a tad small for my hands, but there are few really good solutions that I've found that do the job. title: Not a holodeck, a holo-phonebooth. Still plenty cool.
text:
I’ve given it a couple days, and I’ll try to keep it short.

Yes: It’s amazing. VR is amazing. if “being in a game” appeals to you as a concept, you will love it. I’ve only had short stints with the Vive and Oculus; but it doesn’t take long to figure, this is the best headset – when it tracks right. It’s by far the most comfortable, and with the best screen, resolution be damned. Black levels are great, colors pop nicely, and the lack of “screen door” is huge. The other two are sharper, but always look like LCD screens. 1080p isn’t great, but this headset is. Except for headphone issues, it’s perfect – while seated, or standing in ONE place.

Meh: cables, welcome to cable hell, there’s no way to make this orderly while in use (Neat people may hate). PS camera cable is only 6ft – boo. So it goes, first-world-problems right?

Nope: the tracking is not adequate. Take more than a step in any direction, jitters; extend your arms too far, jitters; turn around, jitters. Everyone who uses this with a Move game will exceed the limits of the tracking within moments. As soon as you become enthusiastic enough to test the limits of the move (by moving), it fails. You do learn the “rules” of where you should hold your limbs, so they can play nice with the sensor range, but this is the opposite of immersion. The interface doesn’t “transport” your arms they way it does your eyes. You can’t count on it to work, so basically any standing game that requires reflexes is likely a no-go with the move [I’d love it if I had to eat those words]. Note that all the real games such as: Rigs, Eve, or Drive Club (i.e. not “experiences”) are using the dual shock.
The PSVR achieves VR visually, but not physically – the tracking sinks that.

Sony selling this in a bundle without move controllers isn’t about you already having them (you don’t, they know you don’t). It’s because the PSVR does not REQUIRE them (hint here). The good games, that we might get, when we’re sick of being batman, will likely not use them. Aside from not being batman you’ll probably be fine without them. Sit down man.

So here it is: VR is awesome, it looks great. The level of immersion will probably exceed your expectations. However, all the wild, amazing games of your VR dreams (Lightsabers!, boxing!, Fruit Ninja!) will either miss this generation of PSVR, or suck a butt.

The games are pretty good, but that’s a different review.

Also: I have a surround sound set up, and I just use that instead of headphones. It’s fine.

title: Great value for a good keyboard
text:
If you are comparing this to a > $200 keyboard, this may not meet your needs but for the price, this is really a great keyboard. It has become the rage to have a volume nob usually at the top right corner of keyboards these days. That is fine, I guess, but I prefer what Royal Kludge has done with this board using the nob as a switch for wired, 2.5GHz and the three bluetooth options. In my opinion, this is much more useful than a volume nob, especially when I can use the F-keys for volume just as easily. Using the nob to switch the keyboard from one device to another is not only easier than using the normal FN key + number key to switch between devices but it will provide a quick visual cue as to what device is currently active.

This is a gasket mounted keyboard. I am not a huge fan of a springy gasket keyboard. This is not such a keyboard. It takes a pretty good press to see any plate flex. What it does do is mute the sound of your keys. That along with the polycarbonate plate makes this keyboard a great option for a work environment where other cube mates may be annoyed by a loud keyboard.

The Sky Cyan switches are super smooth and creamy. They are Royal Kludge's own branded switch and a great option for those who like a linear switch with a great feel. I prefer a top loaded tactical switch so I did replace the installed ones with something of my own choice but I will likely find a good use for these switches. They really are good. One thing to note, they are really tight in the PC plate and will take some effort to remove.

I gave this a 4 star review but for the price and features, it really would be a 4.5 star keyboard and should be one of your top considerations for a keyboard in its price range.

title: Weird Issue with the Playability vs. Ages
text:
I got this for my neice and nephew to enjoy when we visited them last Thanksgiving. As we already had the Buzz controllers, and this was such a cheap game, I figured there was nothing to lose. I'll break out the pros vs. cons of this game below.

Pros:
1) Fun Games - The games are generally pretty fun, and the competition can get pretty heated
2) Monkeys - Yup, Monkeys make everything better.
3) Good Buzz Controller Work - The game uses the controllers well

Cons:
1) Strange Difficulty - Some games were way more difficult than others. I'm not talking about adult difficulty, but for kids...I had a 4 year old and an 9 year old, and some games were competitive, others were too difficult for the 4 year old (which caused her to get REALLY frustrated), and some were too easy for the 9 year old.
2) Limited Replay - The 4 year old liked the monkeys but couldn't hold her own in the game, while the 9 year old got bored and didn't want to play any more.

This game was well put together, and caused some laughs on the first time through, but I don't see what group this game really connects to. The 9 year old only wanted to play once, and the 4 year old wanted to play a ton but had real issues with the controls. No disrepect to the developers as you can tell some work went into this game. Close, but no cigar.

title: Pretty Great for the Price
text:
[[VIDEOID:47027ce69dbd678bbe6e15c0ffdaf073]] Just picked up a new PC and decided to get all new peripherals. First, this is a USB headset. If your device supports USB, this will likely work. If your device needs a 3.5mm connection, this is not for you. I never have any luck with those, so I have to stick with USB. In my recording software I had to select specifically the HeaTal to get the microphone working...Which I assume is the issue the other reviewer had. I didn't have any issues with this working in Movavi, Zoom, Google Meet, or any of the games with voice chat I tried it out with. It's a pretty nice all around headset.

Pros:
Surround/7.1 - The virtual surround mode on these is really very impressive. I had been using regular headphones while gaming and honestly had no idea the sounds could actually come from locations other than just left or right. Can be activated or deactivated with the remote, and you can absolutely hear the difference.
Mic - Mic is really good for this price range. There isn't any clipping, and it can be muted easily with the in-line remote. It can be removed from the headset, and the in-line mic can be used (that's not very good, though). No complaints...Will make it easy to sync my audio when doing a recording.
Lights - VERY SUBTLE. Just a simple light on each earpiece. It's not too much. Won't even warrant a second glance...So...Perfect for an adult. Haha
Cable - Length is really long. Can easily run this to my computer and still sit back in my chair during a gaming session.

Cons:
Remote - It's kinda big. I mean..It's nice that the buttons and sliders are easy to access, but it could have probably been shrunk down to about half the size. I do like that it is higher up on the cable. It won't be clacking against the desk or being dragged around.

Overall I am pleased with this headset. I didn't want something flashy, it sounds great, and the mic is much better than I expected. Will absolutely keep this one for myself instead of giving it to my kids. Check the video for mic quality.

title: Great Keyboard, a hidden Gem at a amazing price.
text:
Okay let's face it, most people are aware of the Corsair product line, however most are not aware that a stand for a lot of quality. The K55, is unique in that it offers many aspects that high-end keyboards possess, like keeping the cost is very reasonable amount. In the last year these keyboards have gone from over $100 just about 50. The changes only to about because new enhanced keyboards have come out. That does not take away from the fact that this is an outstanding keyboard

Pro's
The Corsair comes with a lot of options, the keyboard itself is soft and very quiet. But extremely responsive. This would be an amazing keyboard to upgrade from a stock keyboard. As the difference for a average keyboard to this one is extreme. If your computer is keyboard to a high and two or $300 keyboard it may not meet the mark but it definitely is high quality and increases gameplay quite a bit. The keyboard comes with macro keys that are programmable through the keyboard itself.
( special note) it is advised that you go through the Corsair website, and download the ICUE software program, this will allow you to change the colors more dramatically and customize the keyboard macro settings and many others. This is the same software used for high-end keyboards but is compatible with this keyboard as well and recognizes it 100%. Having the ability to use the software to adjust color, brightness, frequency, and just about anything you can do with the keyboard. You can also program macro settings much easier through the software. It comes with six macro buttons that are fully programmable, meaning you can use shortcut keys, links to software or other websites including e-mail, just about anything you can input into a line to access a file, or destination is possible, especially if you are using the software it's much easier.
If you look at the reviews, when the Corsair originally came out, you will see that it was a contender for one of the top keyboards. Of course as technology changes so does advancement and keyboard technology. I was impressed by the software itself, because it compares itself very much to how integrated software on alien computers are. Allowing a lot of control over the keyboard. Let's get to the keys, they are placed in the original configuration, except that the macros that are on the left side of the keyboard extending the keyboard with by about 2 inches. It comes with a wrist rest, that may be suitable for those with average sized hands. The keyboard seems sturdy with very little flexibility and has risers at the backlit keyboard for adjustments. It has the mediator keys as well as a volume that is fully compatible with Windows 10, and I am assuming all the way back to Windows 7. it should be noted, that there are color variations possible to the software which allow the standard keyboard and other aspects of the keyboard to be in different colors SAME time or you can choose one color for the entire keyboard.

Cons:
There is not much you can say in a negative way against this keyboard. So I'm going to sort of nitpick at some of the smaller aspects of the keyboard.
The key spacing is normal, however having the macro keys takes a little bit time to it just to the width of the keyboard if you are not used to it. I found myself reaching to the first macro key as opposed to the escape key several times with the learning curve because my hand was noticing that was the edge of the keyboard and above is normally the escapee however the macro key is located at the edge now.
One aspect that I did find is a con but it was not large enough to give it a minus star, is the media keys and the volume keys are not lit up. Not sure why they would did not do that's, and the addition keys at the top for other controls are also not let. Only the keyboard buttons itself and the macro keys are lit as well as the number key. it's not a dealbreaker but it definitely could've been something they could have added perhaps the ergonomics of the hardware did not make it possible. The wrist rest, is a little on the short side for someone like me that has larger hands I find just barely very top of the rest my hands are able to touch due to it being the size that is. Why the rest is almost 4 inches, it seemed a little short for me but I think the average person should have no problems I have to wear extra-large close if that helps on the review so it should be fine for most people.

Overview:
As of April 2019, this keyboard goes between $45 and $49 on the average. If purchasing through Amazon you can find it with free shipping. I really enjoyed the fact that the keys are quiet, in any kind of noisy environment of the moderate nature you would not hear the keys at all. Even late at night I was typing and found it was not noticeable at all compared to a standard keyboard. I did not think was fair to compare this keyboard to anything newer because at the time it was released it was a very good keyboard, that came with outstanding setups. The fact that you can acquire free software on Corsair's website to give the keyboard the look and feel you want, because it is fully customizable makes it a definite winner. I've seen and used tire and keyboards, and this definitely puts it at the competition level. However with new technology the keyboard itself is slightly behind. But only because newer more expensive models exist. In the course airline there have been several improvements on newer keyboards but I do not think they eliminate the fact that this is a great keyboard. I would say it's a moderate level gaming keyboard, that has a plus of having macros which does help for certain gaming activities. I do wish the volume level controls as well as the media controls were lit, as often times media buttons are used as a shortcut to a quick action. Not having them lit and having the keyboard lid itself makes it very hard to see those controls without squinting to figure out which one is the proper control. I think at this Corsair had had fully lighted keys including the media and volume, it would have definitely would raise the competition level on newer keyboards that include this feature. As noted above it's not a dealbreaker but it would've been nice had they simply added this small feature perhaps there was a reason they were able to.

Closing thoughts, yes if you're looking for a entry level to medium level gaming keyboard this will definitely be one you would like to have. At that price level right now around $50 or less, it is a steal to get into the gaming keyboard market. When looking on the Internet standard keyboards run around $35-$40 super $10 more you can end up with a very high and keyboard that has many features that are not included on the base keyboard. title: Amazing series and definitely worth your time (and money)!
text:
Sort of an interesting "game" to review, given that for its price, especially if you are new to Halo (kind of hard to believe given that I have loved Halo for the last 13 or so years). As for the content you get Halo: CE with both original/remastered graphics, Halo 2 with both original/remastered graphics, and both Halo 3 and Halo 4 in their original graphics. All are in 60 fps at 1080p if your screen supports it. As you play through, the graphics in 1 and 2 are beautiful, as well as 4 (even though techincally the remastered graphics of 2 are now better than 4's, I prefer the graphics in 4 the most) and then there is 3...On a straight play through if you continue through the games, you may find Halo 3 from a graphical stand point to be left behind, given that it has a major drop out as it has not received the HD graphic overhaul the first two have had. Other than that you can play solo/co-op on all missions, and ALL skulls are available for use out of the box. Additionally, terminals are now hidden and available for achievements in all 4 games and skulls are hidden for achievements in the first three games. Guaranteed the nostalgia and butterflies you will re-experience as you go through the iconic moments in the early Halo games will be worth the money alone.

Additionally you will get access to the Halo 5 multiplayer beta from Dec 29-Jan 18th, which I am definitely looking forward to. You also get free access to watch Halo Nightfall, which is still be released progressively. It details the journey of Agent Locke who will be a major hitter and likely playable character in next year's Halo 5: Guardians. It is very well done from the episodes I have watched thus far, a better series in my opinion than Forward unto Dawn was.

Lastly, you get the multiplayer. Despite what many of complained, and complained...and complained about, they are fixing the online play. Since getting the game on Black Friday, I have had only one problem getting into an online match, and that was before the last 3 updates which have majorly improved play. Now I don't have to wait anymore than I do for Halo matches back on the 360. Many of the maps are either true to their original forms in 1-4, or they have been updated and modernized. Its a real throwback getting to play some of the maps, like Lockdown, from Halo 2 any old fan will instantly feel at home in. Currently the only ranked matches are Halo 2, but they are updating every few days.

The controls now, are a major learning curve, at least as I found. I still have a hard time remembering that I can't just sprint in 1-3, lol, often resulting in death. They do have a controller setting, I forget the name off hand, that you can set so that the controls remain the same through all 4 games, which makes it vastly easier, given that until 3 you won't have any useable items like the pop-up shields or grav-lifts, and you won't have armor abilities until you play on 4 (which I believe means you won't use X or left bumper till 3 or 4). Makes for more smooth game transition and only a quick glance at what game you are playing, depending on the play list.

If you are worried, the campaign alone is worth it, but if you are only in it for the multiplayer, it is far to difficult to tell if it will work for you specifically.

Lastly, the game does require 90gb, at least for the digital download version, I'm not sure about the disc version. It took me forever to download the entire game (most of 2 days and based on my download speed, it shouldn't have actually taken more than 1.5 hours...). So be sure you have good internet and time on hand before you play. The multiplayer will also have 4+ updates you will now need before even jumping online, though they might all be combined for first timers now.

See you online!

title: Just what I needed! Better than I hoped! Worth the money!
text:
I have one of the older Kindles and the only complaint that I have had over the years is that while traveling or at night, I can't read without some kind of light. Of course I have purchased various independent lights that either snap-on or attach to my old case, but this also means keeping up with two things (the Kindle and the light). So I finally asked myself "wouldn't it be easier to invest in one product that would offer both protection and light"? So I purchased this case and have not been disappointed! I'm glad I made the investment.

For the cost of the case, you get:

1. A sleek, attractive case that not only looks smart but is extremely functional. This case is made from a leather (a durable material) on the outside, and is well padded (in a charcoal grey material) on the inside. It definitely appears to be well made (sturdy) and seriously protects the device. The device attaches to the case with two prongs that secure it in place. It is pretty easy to attach. The bottom of the case is open, so you can access the area for the charger easily. Thus, charging your Kindle while it is in the case.

2. The case (with the Kindle enclosed) is not heavy. You can comfortably fit in your purse, book bag; backpack or briefcase, and it won't weigh your bag down.

3. There is a built in expanding (rubberband) type cord that is attached to the case that will allow you to either keep the case open or closed (as desired).

4. The light conveniently rises out of the top right corner of the case. I will warn you that there were times when it seemed difficult to pull out. (Just be mindful that you don't force it, but instead pull the tab up by the indention provided.) However, once it is up, the built-in light does illuminate the screen (more than I ever thought it would) well. The light cuts on and off with the device, so there are no batteries. The light works off the charge of the Kindle, and you control when you use the light. (I also haven't found that the light drains the battery any quicker normal). The light gives just the right amount of illumination, and isn't so bright as that it will bother others sleeping in the same room. My husband always complained that when I would read at night, in bed, that the lamp (on my nightstand) was too bright and kept him from falling asleep. And when I used the traditional clip on book light when traveling in a car, he use to complain that my book light was too distracting. He actually doesn't seem to be distracted or bothered by this gem. Perhaps because it seems to be more defused or softer.

In the end, I don't regret my purchase. I definitely got more than I had hoped and would definitely recommend this case. It is affordable and the benefits outweigh the cost. 5 stars!

title: Crapped out on me at the 11mo mark
text:
I just thought I'd write another review (don't know where my original one is) and update things. The right eye's OLED went bad on me right before the first year of use had completed. Emagin has absysmal customer service. It's difficult to get strait answers from them or seemingly impossible to get return phone calls even to set up an RMA for looking at the unit and providing an evaluation.

Their rough minimum price over the phone to replace the right eye display was as high as the total price I'd originally paid. Does that make sense? Well, it does if you consider their first couple production runs were of very low quality & reliability and they were unloading them at less-than-cost as a mass test to find out exactly what kind of useable lifespan the OLEDs have. I suspect the early runs turned out something like 33% of the OLEDs having a lifespan under 18 months. I doubt they had exact figures since not many had been produced yet and none of them had been used for that long.

If it's a certain percentage of OLEDs that will go bad and the rest have potentially decades of use, then Emagin needs to pony up and either offer refunds or free servicing of the bad units. That is the honest, ethical thing for a corporation to do. Without disclaimers stating the reliability and life-expectancy of your $700 unit might be less than a year, this company is just begging for a class action suit.

Also worth noting, prior to their military contracts coming on line in the last few years, they began abandoning their support services to regular consumers. Employees were rapidly leaving the company and insiders told me the CEO and CFO (who are a married couple) spent most of their time on vacation or at bed & breakfasts, or something. They were practically never around and living high-on-the-hog off the sudden revenues from the Z800 sales.

So we regular customers saved this company from oblivian, helped them be in a place to eventually get the mil contracts, and this is how we're treated in return. Buyer beware.

title: Not for 4k gaming. Downgrade to reach 4k resolution is nauseating
text:
This isn't the console to buy if you're interested in playing in 4k. As of October 2017, I would not recommend buying this console unless you're only going to play video games in 1080p. I bought the Xbox One S about 2 weeks ago to hold me over until the Xbox One X comes out. Yes, I know I was only going to own it for a month but whatever, it's already been returned and I'll just keep my original X1 and not play in 4k.

Having owned Xbox 360 (x2), Xbox One, Xbox One S, PS4, PS4 Pro, and a gaming PC, I can say that it's not gonna cut it for 4k. What put me over the edge is the new Shadow of War game. When plugged into my 4k display, the game looked grainy, fuzzy, had no textures and overall made me nauseous just playing it. I also noticed the same thing with Battlefield 1. I knew it couldn't be the display since everything looks great on my PS4 Pro and when outputting 4k on my PC. Thought maybe it was the game but after downloading Shadow of War on PC, the difference was clear. Even in 1080p on PC, the game just looks 100x better. Textures, shadows, lighting, cutscenes, everything was so much sharper. I was originally questioning Shadow of War since I read such good things about the visuals but after playing on PC, I won't even bother going back to my Xbox version until the X1X comes out.

I knew that it wasn't the game and that the Xbox One S just couldn't handle it. Even back on a 1080p tv the game was less than stellar and obviously developers are pushing out content better than what the original hardware can handle. This is truly a shame since many people who own this console will install a new game expecting the latest graphics and be thoroughly disappointed. Had I not been able to return it, I would have sold it immediately for whatever I could get.

Aside from hardly "upscaling" to 4k, the console is great. Smaller and quieter than the original Xbox One. It's got a really nice design and it felt faster just browsing menus and navigating the dashboard. Unfortunately, I have about 85 games on my HDD so playing games is what I do. I knew the S wasn't really an "upgrade" but it was definitely disappointing to see a console that advertised upscaling and HDR capability to look so awful. Many say you won't notice a performance increase with the S but I immediately noticed a performance DECREASE.

If you want to play games on a 4k display, I would definitely recommend the Xbox One X or the PS4 Pro. However, for the money and the fact that a new Playstation isn't coming until 2019 at the absolute earliest, I'd suggest a Xbox One X.

Hope this review helps. I was really excited about this console and wanted to love it but after seeing what it can do with the latest games, it's clear it's not meant for 4k.

text: I am an avid player of HOS games. As an amateur player, I struggled with HOS-heavy games, but have moved to the more complicated HOS/puzzle/inventory object puzzle games with story lines. I get tired of demons and evil villains, and several games that I purchased only lasted a couple of hours -- not enough scenes or puzzles to justify the money spent. This game, however, is quite lengthy. A complex story involving the writer Hawthorne and his ancestral connections to the Salem Witch Trials send you through locations in time from the 1800s to the 1600s, seeking answers to the mystery. HOS are well rendered. Puzzles to enter doors, etc. are varied in type and level of difficulty. Object gathering is sufficiently difficult to present a challenge. The added bonus is that if you want to know more about the background of the trials and the individuals involved, the information is provided; but you aren't forced to stop to read historical information if all you want to do is play the game. Each scene provides two specific hidden objections -- one to increase hints and the other to unlock bonus games at the end. The unlocking is a challenge. Like other games of this sort, there is a lot of moving back and forth between locations hunting for clues, but the locations are very interesting. I truly enjoyed this game and would highy recommend it and the other Midnight Mysteries titles as well.

title: A design flaw of the keyboard is a huge problem
text:
I am making these comments as a non-gamer. It may be that this keyboard is made specifically for gamers and not meant to be used by anyone else. However, I have owned for some time another brand of gamer keyboard that I use regularly, and it doesn’t have the design flaw that this keyboard does.

Pros

1. It's appearance is attractive, especially the fact that it lights up in blue when plugged in.

2. This keyboard comes with a mouse, and the mouse is also very attractive. It lights up in blue and red when plugged in.

3. This keyboard is both full size and compact in design.

4. The price is reasonable.

Cons

1. A design flaw of the keyboard is a huge problem! I have been typing on a computer keyboard for 40 years. And on every keyboard I have ever used, the Enter key is one key to the right of the Single-Quote/Double-Quotes (“Quote”) key. When you want to press the Enter key, you simply lift up your right pinky finger and move it over one key. Inexplicably, this keyboard includes an extra key between the Quote key and the Enter key! I cannot state strongly enough how enormous a negative this is. There may be some reason for gamers to have a keyboard designed this way, but the keyboard is useless for everyone else. It is simply unusable to me. As a touch typist, the first time I used it, I reached my finger to hit the Enter key and was shocked when nothing happened. I wasn't looking at the keyboard, and for several additional, frustrated taps, I tried again and again to engage what I naturally assumed was the Enter key. Then I looked at the keyboard, and I couldn't believe my eyes. I was hitting an alien key between the Quote key and the Enter key.

Why would anyone design a keyboard this way? If I tried to train myself to use this keyboard, I would quickly develop repetitive stress injury. It is much too far for my pinky to comfortably stretch to reach the Enter key.

Again, this keyboard may be designed specifically by gamers for gamers. But if you are not a gamer and just are looking for a glow-in-the-dark keyboard for a reasonable price, I highly recommend that you look elsewhere.

title: Freedom comes at a price
text:
After playing Batman: Vengeance, it was an exhilarating change to have a protagonist who could fall off the side of a building and survive. My first impressions were: freedom!

But freedom comes at a price. Superman: Shadow of Apokolips is the first of its kind to allow you to play Superman with all of his abilities and in a fully rendered three-dimensional environment, but there are clipping errors and strange forced perspectives that ultimately dampen the game's enjoyment.

The plot is a loosely connected series of events involving the extra dimensional arch villain, Apokolips. Through his minion, Canto, he sets up a series of military-style attacks with "Apokoliptian technology" that he provides to Lex Luthor. Lex eventually sets a series of super villains free from Stryker Prison, including Livewire, Parasite, and Metallo. Or just Metallo's head in this case.

Lex is provided with a cadre of Interbots, strange goggle-eyed guys in masks. But don't worry, they're robots, so Superman can punch them without any gore. I was willing to accept the old G.I. Joe chestnut (i.e., "we have powerful guns, but let's run up to the bad guys and smash them in the face with our rifle butts!").

Punching Interbots is decidedly unsatisfying. Killing Interbots can be amusing at first. Setting them on fire with heat vision causes them to run around, arms flailing. They will sometimes run away, screaming in mechanical voices "This unit is compromised" or something like that. And yet, there's no feeling of Superman's awesome strength. When he hits Interbots, I want to see them go through walls, not just bounce around like rag dolls.

And there are so MANY of them. Superman fights Interbots, Interbot tanks, Interbot missle launchers, Interbot troop transports, Interbot gun emplacements, Interbots with jet packs, and Interbot helicopters. I don't ever recall seeing this many Interbots in the Superman cartoon.

Because of the sheer number of opponents, certain tactics are encouraged over others. Superman has a wide variety of abilities, including his x-ray vision, heat vision, super breath, super speed, flight, and super strength. But his best ability is an area attack slam that drops him at high speed onto the ground, knocking back and destroying everything in sight. This ability was more useful than punching Interbots. So suddenly, Superman becomes a living torpedo. Not necessarily a bad thing, but hardly representative of the Superman cartoon.

The game looks exactly like the movie, rendered in cell-shaded animation. All the voices actors are present, including Lori Petty as Livewire and Malcom McDowell as Metallo. But even those villains aren't the type who can go punch for punch with Superman.

Of all of the villains, only Livewire can fly. Superman slowly regenerates his damage and his super abilities. This means that if he is significantly harmed, you can just fly him away to a safe place and heal there. When fighting Metallo, I did this several times, while Metallo patiently waited down on the ground.

But I don't want to put the game down entirely. The game's plot is entertaining and even has a few twists. When the villains do show up, they are fully realized. I had a difficult time beating Livewire so I had plenty of opportunities to hear her wax poetic about electricity. I can't stand Lori Petty (except for her role in Tank Girl), but she really does act her heart out mocking Superman. Metallo does the same thing. There's a lot of entertainment value in just listening to them mock Superman. Superman returns the favor by talking to himself. Over and over and over. It gets annoying.

In terms of gameplay, there are a few high points. Superman must achieve the random feat of strength - plugging a damn, struggling through a wind tunnel. The game represents these challenges by requiring the player to tap a button repeatedly. Sadly, that mechanic isn't used enough.

The parts of the game that were most challenging (and sometimes frustrating) are the timed events. In essence, Superman must run an obstacle course before time runs out. If he fails...the screen goes white.

OH NO, SUPERMAN MUST BE DEAD!

Ahem. Given that Superman is near immortal, it's difficult to comprehend losing the game because, say, he didn't successful stave off a wind tunnel. So what? Superman would probably end up destroying the fan behind him without a scratch on him. Batman's mortality is precisely what raises the stakes - in Superman, it's hard to feel a sense of urgency for a man of steel.

At one point, Lex releases Metallo and encourages him to go after Superman. But Metallo, a cyborg, was originally created by Lex Luthor and ultimately betrayed by him by removing Metallo's head from his body. The first order of business for Metallo is to go after Lex.

The best part of the game is when Metallo shows up at Lex's office.

LEX: "Hello, Metallo. I was expecting to you."
METALLO: "Good, now stand right still while I remove YOUR head from YOUR body."
LEX: "Mercy?"

Lex nods towards Mercy, his female bodyguard who is carrying a large machinegun.

METALLO: "Not even if you beg."
LEX: "No you idiot, I mean her, behind you."
METALLO: "Do you seriously think I'm going to fall for-"

And that's when Mercy cuts loose with her machinegun, inflicting absolutely no damage whatsoever to Metallo. Unfortunately, Superman steps in at that point. It's telling that the best part of the game is a cut scene.

Overall, Superman: Shadow of Apokolips is an excellent realization of everyone's favorite superhero. Unfortunately, the game developers had difficulty providing challenges for the man of steel.

I am a makeup artist. That means that I use all sorts of makeup from drugstore to high level professional. There are many things about eye shadow that I look for which determine if it is something I can recommend.

HOW THIS COMES
This came with no padding, no protection in a plastic mailer with no bubble cushioning. There is a plastic sheet over the surface of the eye shadow and no mirror in the case. There is no brush.

COLORS
The colors are beautiful. They have nuances that are very difficult to capture on camera. There are matte and shimmer colors- some of which are duochrome- something I look for in shadows.

HOW TO USE THESE
These eye shadows (like almost all other brands of shadow from professional down to drugstore) are best used with a very good eye primer. That will keep them in place and keep them intense too. The only eyeshadow I have ever come across which can be used without a primer and great success is Viseart.

QUALITY
These eye shadows are on a par with the high end cosmetics you find in the more expensive sections of makeup departments. They have a good amount of pigmentation and are velvety smooth too including the mattes.

MATTES
The mattes are not chalky, but are smooth and velvety. They show up well but again, these are best used with a primer.

SHIMMERS
These are some of the most gorgeous shimmer colors I have seen in a while. The collection compliments each other beautifully and look stunning on the eyes and even just in swatches.

ANY ISSUES
I have very sensitive eyes and these shadows did not cause any burning, watery eyes, or irritation of any kind the two days I wore them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This set of eye shadows is gorgeous. For the price, it is excellent quality and is on a par with shadows much more expensive than these are.

MY RATING
I LOVE these shadows. The colors are gorgeous, quality excellent, and performance above most other shadows in this price range- just be sure to get a good eye shadow primer.

title: A Few Frustrations But Overall Great Gaming Experience So Far (And Some Things I Wish The Instructions Said)
text:
My entire family is into gaming and other applications that use headphones and speakers, so I was very interested in try out the Siberia P800 series wireless gaming headphones. There are a lot of excellent highly technical reviews out there for these, but I intend to approach these headphones for someone who is not as into gritty tech details as they might be into practical every day applications.

I am writing this review for those who really want to know about products prior to purchase. I am as detailed as I can be without being overly so, because I want to provide information that I would like to know before purchases. This is an expensive purchase, so it deserves some explanation and time given to research.

WHAT COMES IN THE BOX?
The box that these come in is excellent. It is sturdy and you can keep it for storage of the extra cords and parts if you like. Inside the headphones come carefully pressed into a molded insert. It comes with a wireless transmitter box, every cord you might possibly want to connect it to the Playstation, PC,or Xbox. It also comes with a mobile cable and analog cable for use with TV or mobile device.

The startup guide is, well, let me say really not as good as it should be with an expensive set of headphones like this. For visual learners, you might have some issues unless you are a real techie. There are no pictures of the back of the transmitter box or of the back of the playstation (or other items) you want to connect to so if you are not really good at understanding what goes where, you might have to look up online somewhere how to hook this up to your console or other devices.

WHAT ARE THE HEADPHONES LIKE?
The headphones themselves have a cushioned top and small ear covers on them. The retract and get slightly bigger, but not a huge amount. The top is cushioned and they hold onto the had pretty well, at times feel a bit tight. That will loosen up over time, I am sure.

The left ear pad has a retractable mic in it. When the mic is turned on, a red ring lights up. The disc on the outside of the left ear pad also twists off and that is there the lithium battery is put. When you want to replace, you quickly twist off the cover, replace the battery and you are good to go. There are two arrows that line up for you to replace the cover quickly so you don't have to fumble with it in a hurry to continue your game.

The right ear side has the on off switch on it located just slightly toward the back of bottom of the circle. If the ear pad was a clock with 12 at the top and 6 at the bottom and 9 toward your front with these on, it is about at 5 o'clock. To turn it on, you press for about a minute or so. The switch will light up. If you want to turn on the mic, you tap the same switch once and the mic goes on. Tap again and it goes off.

On the right ear side, there is also a control. It is a wheel which controls volume, but when pressing it, will change the menu on the transmitter box. Then if you move the wheel it will scroll the menu.

The ear pads do fold flat which makes them a bit easier to store when not in use.

I also find that the longer I use these, the more comfortable they seem to become- I imagine they will continue to loosen up over time.

HOW DOES THE TRANSMITTER BOX WORK?
I tested these headphones out on a PS3. I found very little on the internet about using these headphones with a PS3, so knowing that many still use the PS3, I wanted to test using that gaming console first.

SET UP WITH PS3
Optical cable- plug in to optical out on PS3 in back then plug into optical in on the back of the transmitter box.
USB- plug in mini USB side of the cable to the transmitter box and plug the regular USB side into the front of the PS3

POWER - this is optional. The power plug can be plugged in where it says DC but keep in mind that means the transmitter box will be on at all times. If you prefer that it turns off when your PS3 is off, then don't use it. The advantage of the power plug is if you want your battery to charge up when the unit is not on, you can have it plugged in for that. Once done, you can still remove the power plug until needed again.

SIDE SLOT
This package comes with an additional battery. One battery had a single bar of charge on it and the other had two bars of charge on it. So, while using on, the other is charging in the box. I found that with the power plugged in, it took about 45 minutes to reach a full charge or so. One battery took almost an hour. The battery pushes in and locks into place while charging, and then if you push on it again, it will dislodge and come out so you can use it and replace with the other one if you like.

FRONT PANEL
The front panel has a white light up design. It shows the battery charge, that the headphones are on and if you are using gaming and voice and the balance of the two. There is a dial on the right and a back button to the left of that. When turning on the headphones, I get a light that shows they are on then a quick large display of battery power left in them, and then it goes to the screen that shows me PS3 and how much volume is being used at that point. It will also show me the current battery charge of the battery that is charging on the side of the unit too so I can keep track of when it is ready to use should I need it.

The menu is pretty simple to adjust. You press the button to change menu and turn the dial to run through it. There are presets for equalizer and you can also set custom.

WHAT THE DON'T SAY IN THE INSTRUCTIONS
Call me dumb if you want, but although I have programmed computers and done a lot of technical work, I guess I was having a dull moment when I set up these headphones. I could not get them to work. I went through every setting over and over again and just could not make them work right.

Since I have never had headphones on my PS3, (I am the only one who hasn't) I did not realize that I had to change the settings in the sound menu. I should have, but I didn't remember. So, after much looking around, I finally found the setting that has to be changed. There is no mention of it at all in the instruction book. Since this review is geared more toward the casual gamer, I thought you might like to know that small important fact.

You have to go into the PS3 settings menu for sound and pick either the optical sound or you can have both going if you like- through the TV AND headphones. I like to do that when the family wants to be in the room and see what is being played but I want to hear details of sound you normally don't catch on just the TV speakers. You just have to remember to change the settings when you change how you prefer to transmit the sound.

HOW WELL DO THESE HEADPHONES PERFORM?
I am going to have to really work with these for a while to find the ins and outs of them. My first impression of them was awful. I really was disappointed. There was hissing, crackling and all sorts of noise with sound effects on various games. The music seemed fine, but every time there was an explosion or some sort of noise that was supposed to be electronic in nature, the headphones had so much other noise in them it was distracting and annoying. I messed with volume and settings and everything and it just didn't get as good as I thought it should have.

I kept on, however, changing to various games. As I moved through all sorts of different games, I realized that some games must be designed with engines that do not seem to transmit clearly over the wireless headphones. They just are awful. Then other games seemed to be clear and a lot easier to play.

DOLBY
So far, I have had the best results when removing Dolby on all of the games I have tried. I am not sure if that is because the headphones are designed for 7.1 and the PS3 is designed for 5.1, but it seems to be more muffled with the Dolby on and there are more annoying features that come up with sound effects. I will continue to play with this and see how to make it work if I can. I will update this review at that point. We have several different gaming consoles we can try these with, so over time I will elaborate if I find solutions or differences. The listing on these headphones does specify that it will work on both PS3 and PS4 so I plan to see what I can find out about this over time.

MUSIC
I have watched videos on these headphones and found them to be excellent. I can hear all sorts of nuances that I did not catch on just the TV speaker. I watched them via Netflix and also Bluray on the PS3. Sound was much better than some games. Like I said, however, it could just be the software used when developing some games that does not translate as well into the headphones as others.

I do want to point out, that these are GAMING headphones. They are not going to be the top of the line for music listening, so if that is primarily what you want them for, they probably will not be what you want. For the variety of needs I have on the PS3 of videos to music in games and movies, they are surprisingly good.

MICROPHONE
I have not had the opportunity to test out the mic yet with other players. I will update as that opportunity presents itself and will comment on performance during gameplay.

THE BOTTOM LINE
So far I really like these headphones but have a few issues with them. Some games do not sound right in these at all, and others sound beautiful. That is not always the fault of the headphones, but it does make for annoying experiences in some games. The design of the headphones is nice and I do love how they work when they work well with games. The transmitter is easy to use and battery life seems a bit shorter than 20 hours, but I like the fact that you can keep a battery charging while playing so when you need to replace you can.

I also like that you can opt to have the power on to them while the PS3 is off so you can recharge battery, but then unplug it so that it only turns on when the PS3 is on too.

For the price, I have rated these four stars at this time. As I continue to use them and learn more about them and the ins and outs over time, I will update and amend my rating if need be.

FUTURE UPDATES
I plan to test these out with other games as well on my PC games as well as tablet in the future and will comment on those experiences as well.

GAMES TESTED SO FAR (more coming soon)
Monkey Island (newest one)
Hydrophobia
Zen Pinball
Peggle
Planet Minigolf
Spellunker HD
Beyond Two Souls

title: Educational....
text:
This is a simple game and it doesn't take much to play it. You don't have to think too hard, either, but when not playing the "Top Trump File" can be read to learn more about who/what is on the card. I don't see it being something anyone would want to play on a regular basis, but for occasional play, it's a nice way to spend some time with others and it manages to easily get some education into my children's day. It also helps to pass the time if boredom is there. Even when not playing, it's fun just to look through the cards, at least to me.

To play, someone deals the cards to the players face down. The players then pick up their cards, so only one card is visible. The player to the dealer's left starts and picks any stat on their card to call out. The other players call out that same stat and the best number gets all the cards, which then goes to the bottom of that person's stack. The winner of each round picks the next stat for the next round. The game ends when a player has all the cards, and they win. This can take awhile to play, so the directions have instructions for a quicker version, too, along with details about what to do if 2 players both have the best stat.

Depending on what set it is depends on what stats are included. The "Greek Myths" set has Strength, Magic, Terror, Audacity, and Top Trumps Rating. The "Ancient Rome: Gods and Emperors" set has Strength, Legacy, Terror, Popularity, and Top Trumps Rating. The "Washington DC: 30 Things to See" set has Cost, Visitors per Year, Year Established, Visit Time, and Top Trumps(Must See). They all have a picture of some sort, along with more information about the person/place/etc.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- unless you change your windows XP kernel to use 3 GB VM you cannot play this at all, it will crash on 32 bit with default VM settings.
- also, 1.5 GB of RAM (given nothing else already resident) is realistically the absolute minimum.

Other than that the game is reasonably light on hardware requirements since it is using an old engine. There is some lag when playing but it is server-side and your own hardware won't matter. I would make sure you are on 64 bits and have a decent amount of RAM, 4 GB or so, if you have less you run but it takes endless to swap in new textures as you walk around. title: Arcade Flight Sim in 3D With Wonky Dynamics
text:
I was excited to find a flight sim with both WWI & WWII planes for the PS3. I had hoped this would be a mix of Rise of Flight (PC) and IL-2 Sturmovik (PC or PS3) which allow you to customize the gameplay to make it as realistic or arcade like as you prefer. Unfortunately (for me), the customization is minimal and the gameplay is much like an arcade with some wonky flight dynamics and a story thrown in.

The story is told in comic form and fully voiced. Not the best voice acting or story, but still a nice touch.

The graphics and audio are nothing special. There is constant screen tearing regardless if you use 3D mode or not.

It provides 3D gaming which is nice. The text (subtitles & alt/speed) is not done right in 3D and messes with your eyes during missions...otherwise, the 3D effect is pretty well done. I played 2 missions in 3D but preferred non-3D due to the text and comfort.

Online play ... it's in the game, but I tried to find someone to battle online for two nights and found ZERO people. Don't buy this game if you are mostly or even interested in online dogfights.

If you are looking for an arcade plane game with a story and planes from WWI & WWII, then give this a try for cheap. If you are looking for something more realistic or historical, then go with IL-2 Sturmovik or Rise of Flight.

title: It's cheap because you don't get much for it
text:
This (G413 SE TKL) is a very basic mechanical keyboard with no bells and whistles. If you're looking for something inexpensive in a mechanical kb, this is possibly worth considering, but you can get a lot more for just a little more money. (Check ratings and reviews on a site like PCMag or Wirecutter.)

The good: it's compact, and the mechanical keys are ok. It has key backlighting (with brighness adjustment, see below). That's it.

Not for the not so good:

The keys are a bit stiff, and typing on this is going to take an adjustment. My much more expensive Razer keyboard is a whole lot smoother and has a significantly better feel. (I no longer recommend Razer because their Synapse software is horrible, and is blocked by some corporate IT departments because of perceived vulnerabilities.)

This is not an RGB keyboard (no colors): all you can do is adjust key brightness (using FN + F1/F2) through a few preset levels. You can't customize anything.

(Note that some reviewers complain about the side-by-side key symbols: that's what you get in a backlit mech keyboard, because the middle can't be lit, being blocked by the post. IMO you get used to this pretty quickly.)

Overall I can't recommend this, and I'm still considering returning it to Amazon. I bought this because I needed something "good enough" in a hurry, and it was available and on sale. In retrospect I should have spent a little more to get a better keyboard.

title: This is a really nice TKL keyboard.
text:
I decided recently to upgrade both of my keyboards to mechanical ones, and after doing quite a lot of research, I decided that these BlackWidow TKL linear switch keyboards were the best fit for me with price and performance in mind.

Overall I'm pretty happy: the touch and feel of the keyboard is wonderful (I really prefer the linear switches), the wrist rest is essential and quite comfortable, and the TKL size allows me to position the keyboard near the mouse, which for me is ergonomically much better. (I had been using a Logitech Wave for years, and I'm still a bit surprised by how much better this keyboard is for me overall.)

Downsides? Firstly, these are the keys with the secondary characters not lit: if you want those lit, you have to spend about $30 more to get the PBT keycap upgrade package. (Or you can buy another Razer TKL product, most likely without a wrist rest.) Secondly, I don't like the light under the keys, I think that's quite unnecessary and distracting, actually making it harder to read those unlit characters. Oh, and my pet peeve is the Delete key being the same size as the others: I happen to use it almost as often as I use backspace, and much prefer keyboards where that key is made larger.

Finally, you want to hope you never need Razer customer service. My experience with them has been pretty bad: they're really slow, they don't do what they say they'll do, and it can take several days and multiple attempts to do something that with Amazon takes about 5 minutes. They don't seem to take it seriously enough.
