title: Where's the adventure?!?
text:
I rated this game four stars for fun, but overall three stars based on the fact that it veers so far from the Donkey Kong legacy it does not deserve to have the DK title. Had this been a different character with a different name my disappointment in this game would have been much less--but having a history full of fond memories of the Donkey Kong series I hate to say that this one certainly does not live up to the name. It is very obvious that DK: Jungle Climber was not made by RARE. There is no real adventure incorporated into the game. The concept is new and enticing--Donkey Kong spins on pegs...wooden pegs...stone pegs...iron pegs...ice pegs--they change from level to level. And DK has some interesting new techniques with this game, such as the attack method, and his ability to fly. However, those (and the graphics) are the only perks to the game. The story is average at best. There are very few extras outside the levels, and achieving 100% completion is not worth the time spent. There is a maximum of one bonus barrel in each level (if any at all) and the challenge is always the same--catch bananas in a barrel, whoopee. There are items to collect within the levels, such as the KONG letters, the banana coins, and the DK coin, but they serve no significant purpose other than free men and useless cheats. And don't be fooled by the cover, you cannot play Diddy as you have been able to in past games. If the level manages to actually have a DK barrel, Diddy comes out and sits on DK's back. When DK gets hit, Diddy goes away. My biggest complaint is that I felt that some of the levels were entirely too difficult. Not difficult because of lack of skill, but simply because it would take several times of playing a certain part of the level over and over and over until you figured out the strategy needed to beat it (since DK dies so easily), and by that time you are so tired of the playing the level you're ready to just put the game down for good. I remember spending about 40 men trying to beat one level (and having any more than 20 men is a major feat!)

Overall, I'd have to say if you've been embedded in the DK games of the past, don't expect the same level of activity and fun with this one. If you are new to video games or the DK series, you will probably enjoy this game. But I encourage you to try some of the older Donkey Kong country games, which were developed for SNES but are also available as GBA games and can be played in the DS.

title: Awesome game, open world, tense firefights
text:
I'd never played any of the OFP games before this one and I'm impressed, it has been too long since there's been an approachable military tactical like the GRAW and Rainbow Six Vegas games. One thing you should do if you are only a slightly more than casual player is get a trainer/cheat, otherwise it's too realistic and it seems like you would die a lot as you are expected to work miracles in some missions. It's also not that large of a game in terms of GB's and the missions and number of commands are not ponderously huge like the ARMA games.

The missions are made pretty clear by HQ and you have HUD checkpoints and objectives as well as a map to keep you moving towards the objectives. Commands to your team are easily done with the radial menu in game by pushing the Q button and navigating to your command via the WSAD buttons. This is also how you call in support like mortars, artillery and airstrikes. You can also give commands via the map screen but it's not really recommended as the map is only zoomable to a grid size, not a tactical size. Once you give your command you announce it in the grid coordinates, which seems a little overdone when you are just ordering your team to a point you can see, I can see this making sense for out of visual contact things like the artillery and the like though. A bad thing is that when you order your team to move to a point it seems it takes them a long time to get there or they don't move there when under fire, what's the point of ORDERS then? Another thing is if you have to jump out of a vehicle and run to stay alive your team NEEDS to be ordered to follow you, as if.

Vehicles are pretty straight forward to get into and either drive or be a passenger and you can switch to a swingman view for this if you want. You can only see immediately in front while in swingman/follower view though instead of using the mouse to look left/R/behind so that's a negative aspect of the vehicles. All I saw that you can use is 4 wheel cars, no tanks or planes.

The missions are pretty huge as far as ground to cover and non-planned objectives and there's a good variety of shoot em up focused ones and stealth missions. I'd like to see some city combat situations though instead of the almost total mission time in the mountains/fields. Also I've been in mission and seen the time of day ambient light change which is a nice touch. At times the checkpoint autosaves can be a little too far apart if you do go down but it wasn't a big problem with my God mode trainer. You can also fail a mission by not doing certain things in an allotted time or being detected when stealth is a mission necessity. At times it does seem to be a long time just hiking to your next objective but it leaves vehicles and enemies at good points in between to break it up.

I found the weapons to be accurate graphically and in sound to real assault rifles as I've fired a few of the real things. Also the difficulty in hitting a target seems about right. If you've never fired a weapon at a target you can't possibly know how much skill is involved, it's hard to hit a target at 8 feet with a 9 mm handgun due to many factors and this is also true of any other firearm. So that's not a legitimate gripe.

Overall graphically this is pretty good for the huge environments, It seems to make a nice tradeoff in that respect. Every little thing in the game is not top quality detailed like buildings or vehicles but that's not the real fun of the game anyways. The characters and weapons are nicely done and that's what you see most of the time anyways. I'm not sure how much of a system hog this is as I have a quad core 6600 and an 8800GT and 3GB RAM so most games don't touch my system but it doesn't seem to be unreasonable. It auto detected my system about where it should be at 1680x1050 and it ran smooth at all times. The sound was great, very nice buzzing bullets and helos as well as ambient outdoors sounds.

One thing I'd like is to choose my own loadout, it's pretty ridiculous going to take out an AAA site and not even carrying a heavy weapon capable of taking out the armored AAA vehicles. You have to find one of the crates that are around with different, usually enemy, weapons in them to get what you need at times. I think at least one of your squad should carry a bazooka of some sort at all times. And it would be nice to choose a silencer and a scope other than a red-dot, look at the guys in Iraq and you'll see that at least one of a squad has an ACOG 4x scope. Usually it's the commander, which you are in this game, that has that. So you are at the mercy of what is given to you as far as weapons unless you want to take the crappy but scoped Chinese stuff off of a casualty.

The story is explained in flash/graphics instead of cutscenes at the very beginning of the campaign missions and that's fine. I found the story to be a little unbelievable though as far as Americans fighting for Russia's interests, I don't think anyone in the USA would want Americans doing that. It's hard enough to take Americans dying for ungrateful and undeserving Iraqis, Serbians, Africans and others. Who cares, in terms of strategic US interests, about an island north of Japan anyways? The part where the Chinese invade Eastern Russia is totally believable though, as when you have 1.5 billion people you need a lot of resources and there's a lot of that in E. Russia. The overall story doesn't really intrude on the game though and that's a good thing, this is just a straight tactical military simulator and that's how you look at it, one objective to the next.

Overall I loved this game and will probably play it again, especially since you can choose individual missions once you've finished the campaign or just go get a full save game on the net. Obviously this is going to have add-on packs like OFP1 did so it is a game that will last a long time. I'm getting the OFP1 GOTY edition which has all the add on packs included after playing this one, it's great and recommended!

title: Good Content & Solid Stable Game
text:
As some reviewers have mention if you own Mortal Kombat (2011) game some of the characters will feel like they have a similar style, However the animations are different and combos are different. Let's face it in some fighting games they will have multiple people who feel the same!(I am talking to you Street Fighter) Still love it though.

GOOD/PROS:
1. The story for a fighting game is pretty damn good. The story feels like a DC Comic story. If DC would have allowed for a higher rating, let's say M rating, I feel like they could have shown more story, like how Superman lost control because of the "drugs". Much more emotion are captured through animations, video, and dramatic music versus characters narrating or explaining what happen earlier. 4.0 / 5.0
In order to get a five it would need a longer story which could have been done.

2. The graphics are nice, nothing more nothing less. You will not see photorealistic graphics or high level of physics. 3.2 / 5.0

3. Sound is always half the experience in movies / video games, the other half is of course cinematics. The soundtracks could have been better and louder in some parts more than others but there really was no room to put in. This is a great story however not enough emotion to drive it. So all you have left is background music for different stages. I think it's appropriate and it fits well. 4.0 / 5.0

4. Characters all feel like they should, example Superman move sets are all punches! He only knows how to use his fist which goes well with him. Superman has no need to execute advanced fighting techniques because he is known for always holding back. Batman has a head-butt, an appropriate parry since he is known for a master of parry's. Every characters fighting style felt appropriate according to that character. The voices are done by their original voice actors for the most part that was pleasant :) 5.0 / 5.0

Total AVG = 4.05

CONS/ BADS

1. Not enough custom skins to unlock, come on give me more! This is our only way to express ourselves while playing online.

2. Needing an IOS device to unlock certain aspects of the console version..... WHAT KIND OF #### is this? Not all of us have an ios. You wont be missing anything critical from the game but still we love to unlock everything they made this more... inconvenient.

Conclusion

Good game, you can expect solid 5-7 hours of story mode campaign. This won't be a game where you can invest a few dozen hours like Mass Effect, Skyrim or so on on story mode. After you beat the campaign you do classic battle mode with each character if you desire to see a short clip showing a small side story. After that you go online meet some friends and do different types of matches. Not much replay value afterwards, you just go online and find a new challenger to push you :). That's all there is to a fighting games. My rating was based on rating the Fighting Game Genre, which in my opinion is a proper way to rate games. You compare sports video games to sports video games. FPS to FPS in order to have more consistency in rating.

title: GOOD RPG
text:
Reading some of the other reviews here I was feeling I had made a mistake in buying this game. Truth is I got quite involved in it from beginning to end.

As some other reviewers have noted, about halfway through the game narrows down to a single purely hack-n-slash non-stop all-out war but a few things keep the game interesting: The character will keep leveling up, so directing his skill points and perks provides variety to the otherwise repetitive and seemingly endless confrontations. Almost every locale has its own types of foes and tactics that work on one type of foe may not work on another. Inventory can be very important in this game, particularly enchanted armor and weapons, and partly because there is no prohibition against changing armor and weapons during a battle. At times inventory management is the name of the game.

I purchased a French edition to get practice in French but wound up playing the English version because the French edition still had English voiceovers anyway. The French edition does a complete install to your hard drive and once installed you can run the game without the CD in your CD drive. Using the multi player option on a home network is thus facilitated.

As others have noted, the game plays only 800X600 resolution in non-zooming isometric view but the graphics were colorful and imaginative. The characters seem to be fully 3D and even cast shadows. The result is that this game is a lot easier on your eyes than the Infinity Engine games like Baldur's Gate and Icewind Dale.

Miscellaneous: Sound track music is good though not memorable. Spell effects are not terrifically spectacular but there is an interesting variety to them. Game ran well on an older AMD Duron driven system with FX 5200 graphics board under Windows 98SE although I had to turn off overclocking on the graphics card to get to El Calle Perdido. Perhaps because it is part 3D, the game make considerable demands on the graphics subsystem and overclocking the FX 5200 notably improved the rate of motion and action.

title: Run & Gun = Run & Die
text:
Socom is a very cool game. I was (and perhaps still am) a [[ASIN:B0016B28WU CoD4]] online junky. Now I have some fresh new junk to get addicted to.

Why would I need Socom if I already have an online shooter that I'm addicted to? Because Socom is truly different. This is a team tactical shooter and CoD4 is run out into the map and kill as many people as you can shooter.

The key to success (for me anyway) in Socom is "stick together".

You play as either a Commando or a Mercenary. Once in a lobby you can switch teams and during intermissions the game will regularly switch your whole team back and forth from Mercenary to a Commando. You can create about 5 Mercenary profiles and 5 Commando profiles; and you can change the weapon loadouts in game.

There are assault rifles, submachine guns, light machine guns, shotties, sniper rifles, and one extra rifle from a group of 5 that are available depending on whether you're in a clan and what clan you're in (Spain, France, Germany, UK or US).

All of the rifles and the following gear and stuff are available to everyone; I don't think there's any unlocking or leveling up needed. Your rewards for quality play instead are status, medals & stars.

The gear is kind of cool, but I'm pretty sure that the best loadout is the simple one: M67 frag grenades. The missile launchers are effective, but cumbersome. The claymores have to be detonated versus the CoD4 kind that blew up if an enemy walked near it. So for now, I'm sticking to the grenades.

One thing to note is that each weapon needs to be equipped. In other words, there's not a dedicated button on the controller to throw a grenade or switch to a launcher. You need to bring your selected secondary weapons up on a display by pressing O. Once a secondary weapon is selected you can switch back and forth between it and a primary weapon by pressing L1 (no, L1 is not your sight button; sight is up on the D pad...and to get off your sight you must press down on the D pad). (You can custom configure the wireless controller to your own liking if you don't like the default or other presets.)

The attachments for your weapons are plentiful: scopes, regular and laser sites, silencers, bipod and grenade launchers. Each attachment is not available on every weapon. And be careful, a laser sight will give away your position in night games.

Oh yeah, night games...you'll need your nightvision goggles for those. Navigating the maps takes a little getting used to, but as I said earlier, you should be pretty much sticking together with your team...follow them and take a position. That's right...there's some camping to be done here...but be smart: stay in one place too long and you'll be dead faster than you can say WTF!

And speaking of dead, I believe that you only get rewards by playing "ranked" matches. Friendly fire is on and there is no respawning. There are 4 v 4 matches, 8 v 8 and higher; so when you play Socom, in some matches you'll be atop the leaderboard with 2 kills. I personally have enjoyed the two smaller group matches, but that's a matter of preference.

So communicate with your team! Someone on your team is probably familiar with the map. Ask where to go. There's no stupid or noob questions here; the players that I've met got more mad when their team members didn't communicate and use their mics than they did when someone says "what should we do?"

Speaking of the mic, I bought the [[ASIN:B001C4DKG4 Stand Alone]] edition of Socom, because I have the [[ASIN:B0009B0IX4 Plantronics Voyager 510 Bluetooth Headset]] and it works great. But if you want to take advantage of all of the perks (like on screen volume and stuff) that were in the PS3 2.5 firmware update, then you should probably go with this edition that includes the new official PS3 Headset.

This game rocks. Some of the maps according to some of the folks that I've played with are carry-overs from past Socom games. That gives Socom vets a bit of an early advantage. But it won't be long before I'm navigating these maps on point instead of following my team.

Buy Socom if you play online.

Side note on initial game installation: If your PS3 is set to auto-start discs you might need to disable that the first time you plug in the disc. After you put the game in, you'll see two icons on the XMB for Socom; one installs the game, the other starts it. Install the game first. For some reason even after you run the installer, the game installer icon doesn't disappear; just be sure to start that game with start icon going forward. After the installation I got an error message that said my "saved data" was corrupted....so I deleted the Socom saved data from the XMB (NOT the "game" data...the "saved" data) and the error message disappeared.

Another side note that made take away a star in the overall rating: As of this writing, there are major server issues. Load delays. Freezes. Choppy action and more. Slant 6 Games NEEDS to fix these. If you release a game that is online only, you should release it when you are ready to set the bar for online gaming...not be a work in progress.

title: Good, but could be better in some obvious areas.
text:
I've been playing it for a little while now, and I have noticed that it is NOT surprising. Nothing will surprise you or WOW you in this game. It's good; it works; will definitely satisfy your desire to play a golf game on your PC, but...

I figured that they would spend a little more time and put some more effort into the stuff that matters instead of additional customizable details for your player's face and whatnot. Who cares? A scar? Whoop-de-do. 4,000 choices of clubs that all play about the same? Dozens of hats? Big deal.

1) We want the Course Architect! The skate board games have had that ability for years, and has become integral with the games. Why would you put it on SOME TW games and not this one?? Seems really cheap of them to leave it off. Are they going to ask us to buy it as an add-on? Good luck.
2) More natural ball movement and bouncing (i.e. when a real golf ball hits concrete it takes of like a rocket, but in the game it bounces and rolls like its in med rough.)
3) Hitting irons off of the carpet is no better than med rough? Since when?
4) The computer-driven golfer can often get stuck in parts of Central Park course. They choose to hit a ball in the rough with a 3W and it goes 3 feet only to have them turn 180 and hit it with a 3I and go 100 feet -- out of bounds. This repeats until the golfer concedes. The out of bounds on the 18th hole of Central Park green is inaccurate and absurd.
5) The mp3 for the creek/brook sounds like a skipping record.
6) When you play against a better golfer, but have them nerfed to 'novice', they will almost always hit the hole and roll over it if they are more than 10 feet away - you're pretty much guaranteed that. Gets annoying after awhile.
7) The people are obstacles, and seem to have some kind of sticky clothing?? Since when does a ball hit by a driver "land" on a guy's shirt? Or sort of stick to him and slide down? They people should have no surface and let the ball fly through them -- (most of the time) they would be moving out of the way during real golf.
8) How 'bout adding a golf cart racing secret code or something fun? I know you want it all serious and whatnot, but those that would like to pimp out a golf cart, jump one off a bunker or whatever could seek out the code. Those that are not into that could be none the wiser and still think it serious.

I'm guessing that the "PGA" in "Tiger Woods PGA Tour 07" is what keeps it pretty boring. Oh well, I'll have to look elsewhere for the fun in golf.

title: A review from someone who is actually playing it....not just saying my kid likes it...and a bit of comparison to the 3ds version
text: Love it.  Great graphics, fun modes and lots to do. Terrific voice acting and characters.  I have the 3ds version and the portal works fine with the PS3.  The console version really is a whole lot better than the 3ds version but the 3ds version is more of a platformer, you can store two Skylanders and just swap them out by tapping their icon on the bottom screen and they can jump.  Other than that, the PS3 version is a much more immersive and richer game.  I think this is a game for the whole family to enjoy and I have played a heck of a lot of games since 1978.  Infact, it sort of reminds me of old fashioned Diablo type dungeon crawling (and some Skylanders have similar type abilities) but most of the adventuring takes place in well lit areas and even though the NPCs are cute they are not "sticky sweet" or too childish for adults who just want to experience a fun game. I love the bright colors and the little details like ice forming on the ship...or little puddles on the deck.  And it is FUN. I like buying the character updrades in this version as that is not an option but is automatic in the 3ds version.  Skylanders transferred from the 3ds retain their LEVELS but not their upgrades.  Hats in this version actually have a purpose and can effect stats in many different ways such as making a Skylander faster or better defensively.  In the 3ds version hats just sit on their heads and look cool...lol....no effects at all.  I waited for this version and the figures to become a little more affordable and honestly, it's one of those rare times I wish I had just bought it on release day because it's that good and would have been well worth the price. Finding new figures in the stores is almost impossible now. Good news-- It's ok to buy Skylanders used if you want to or don't have a bunch of cash....this version has an option to reset the Skylander so you can do all its stats, leveling up yourself.  Also...the best thing about BOTH games....you really only have to have 1 giant and a Skylander of each element to play the game effectively and enjoy all the parts.  So...I think that comes down to your giant and 7 of the other elements.  And since you can use Skylanders from the original game, there's lots to pick from and enjoy.  Of course, you'll want more than 8 but it's like eating an elephant---ONE bite at a time will get you there :)  At first I thought the figures were a horrible gimmick idea but now that more and more games on any system are requring you to pay for additional DLC...this is really cool since you have a figure and a game character to show for your money spent.  There's no online mode for the battle arenas....that's the only thing I don't like about this game. I've been fairly dependent on online for quick games with other people for several years so no online battle option feels like a step backwards in gaming.  Other than that, i think the concept is amazing, the game plays very well, the modes mix it up, replay value is strong for each level and for each figure you collect.  I think it's superb and would think anyone who likes games could enjoy this nearly perfect game.

title: One of the best headset available on the market right now

title: Brilliant for fans of the Old Skool CRPG genre of games
text:
The first thing to understand about Pillars of Eternity (PoE) is that it is intentionally designed as a retro, old-skool gaming experience that plays the way CRPGs did in the "classic" CRPG era of Baldur's Gate/Planescape: Torment -- i.e., circa 1998-2000. This refers to the entire *experience* and gameplay, not just the "core". What has been updated is simply the graphic detail and resolution, which is full 1080p. Everything else, especially game mechanics, is a loving recreation of the old skool designs from the classic era. This includes movement, combat, use of text, conversation trees, and so on.

I say that this is the first thing to understand because if you don't understand it, you may be disappointed in the game. The game is not using "modern" or "contemporary" conventions when it comes to computer RPGs -- like you may have seen in the Dragon Age series or the Mass Effect series or Kingdoms of Amalur or what have you. It very consciously is using game design and systems that are from the "classic" era of ~15 years ago, to appeal to players who like those older systems very much, and the kind of gameplay that they permit. If you strongly prefer the more contemporary style of CRPG gameplay, you will probably be frustrated with the mechanics of PoE, again, because it is so old skool.

However, if you very much like the classic design and conventions, PoE is a feast of a game for you. You can micro-manage to your heart's content, engage in blow by blow combat akin of pen and paper games, immerse yourself in deep, textual lore for hours on end in a journey that is interesting, satisfying and rewarding ... if you like the mechanics. For someone who likes that approach to CRPGs, the game will be a fantastic experience, and is not to be missed.

title: Solid heavy tool
text:
Once you pick up this guitar controller, you'll know its more than some cheap toy (which is good, as you'll have that feeling when you pay for it too). This feels more like a well made tool (its made of real wood), but just don't try to plug it in an amp or anything for that matter, as it's wireless. The wireless works very well, as its an officially licensed accessory that doesn't require some odd dongle. Just plug the batteries (included) in and fire up your favorite guitar game. At first its a little tight, but it quickly establishes itself as a smooth and precise controller. Before long the weighty axe starts to be a bit of a pain on the ole back, but since its wireless you can grab a chair even if its across the room.

Style wise it's more of a modern Guitar Hero controller than Rock Band, but it works great in both. It also works great in DJ Hero. The frets and all of the other controls are positioned in the same locations and with similar spacing, but the larger guitar makes it feel more natural and is easier to play for extended periods (as long as the weight isn't an issue). It looks awesome (bonus points if you love orange), and it doesn't look so bad in your living room, which is more than I can say for other controllers. Plus it makes a great home defense tool, as it'll likely create a far bigger knot in the head than any baseball bat.

title: What a Hack Job
text:
The original Army of Two was a fun and unique game. There are not a lot of true co-op games these days and so the original was pretty cool in that way. There was a good bromance between Rios and Salem and stuff that required you to work as a team. There was also a semi-interesting plot, weapon customization and a pretty good variety of locales. Playing the game again, it can be a little easy since everything is kind of slowed down and the bosses get repetitive, but it was still a good game.

40th Day suckered me in with their demo. Based on that, I thought it was going to be a good game. There was a long intro that seemed to hint at a decent plot, improved graphics, new features, better gameplay and a lot more weapon customizations. Then, after the first level, everything went downhill. The plot that they spent so long introducing ended up being totally useless. You have no idea who the bad guy is until the second to last level, and you have no idea why everything around you is happening. After a while it seemed like they just gave up on the plot. The ending of the game is just plain dumb and makes you wonder what they were thinking. It's not like the first one had the most enthralling storyline ever, but compared to 40th Day it was a work of art.

Some new features were cool, like the ability to run (although it is the same button as heal, which leads to you running away from your partner when you try to heal them sometimes), but stuff like the hostage grab rarely ever came up. The morality choice seemed interesting at first, but then slowly tapered off into nothing.

The new weapon customization seemed awesome at first since there was so much to choose from and it was wayyy better than the original game for getting it done quick. But then you start to realize that there is just too much crap there. Dozens of barrels and scopes and stocks that cost thousands of dollars but really don't do much, stupid skins for your guns etc. For some reason, you can buy 57 barrels for the M4 but there are only three pistols. Plus, when you die, it resets to the defaults, which can be really annoying if you want a certain kit to start a level but you keep dying.

I thought this game was an improvement over the first one, but in hindsight it was all smoke and mirrors. Seemed like they had all these ideas and put them in a demo level and then they just went on cruise control from there. The bromance, humor and originality of the first game is sorely missing in this one.

title: Phenomenal
text:
This is an excellent game.. Some people are complaining that it's the same exact thing as Modern Warfare 2.. Overall, it pretty much is, but I don't think that's necessarily a bad thing.. I'm a strong believer in not fixing what isn't broken. MW2 was amazing, as is this game. So far I've invested about 30 hours in this game between campaign, multiplayer and the new spec ops modes, and I still have a long way to go!

In the campaign, you continue on with Soap and Price's story. The campaign is fun, enthralling and action-packed. I played it on normal difficulty and it took me about 6 hours to complete. Again, a lot of people complain about the fact that the campaigns in the COD series are too short, but we don't buy these games for the campaigns, we buy it for the multiplayer.. However, in my opinion, the campaign is still a lot of fun.. From team-sniping with your AI partner to using predator drones, the campaign is still as awesome as ever.

Regarding multiplayer, it seems like it has improved! When it switches hosts I've yet to be dropped out of a game. I also get put into matches pretty quickly. There are also new game modes which are excellent! Team Defender is a variation of capture the flag. There is one neutral flag with no destination for it.. Your objective is to simply capture the flag and hold onto it as much as possible while teammates protect the flag carrier. Then there is kill confirmed, which is a variation of team deathmatch. In this mode, when you kill an enemy you must pick up his dog tags for points. You must also try to retrieve dog tags from fallen teammates before the other team picks them up. Both game modes are very intense and fun to play. In this game, each weapon has its own level so not only do you level up, but your weapons do too. The higher your weapon level, the more attachments and camo you unlock for them. Finally, killstreaks are better than ever! You make a different killstreak with EACH class.. You can also choose between assault, support and perks. It adds an entirely new element of strategy when making your classes.

Finally, there is spec ops mode. Spec ops mode brings back missions like there were in MW 2. I haven't played much of this mode so I don't have much to say on it, but also in spec ops mode there is survival mode! Survival mode alone is worth the price of the game! You can play solo, split-screen or online with 1 other player and you fight off waves of enemies. You can choose from any of the multiplayer maps (which there are plenty of!) and you start off with a pistol and fight off the first wave... Each kill earns you money which can be used at any of the three crates placed throughout the map... A gun crate where you buy guns, an air support crate where you can purchase predator missiles, air strikes, and even AI-controlled delta squad support! Then there is the equipment crate where you can guy frag grenades, flash bangs, turrets, etc. They are usually placed pretty far apart and you only have about 30 seconds between waves, so you need to prioritize what you need for the upcoming wave.. You start by killing foot soldiers in the first wave that take a few shots from a pistol to put down, and before you know it you're fighting attack dogs with C4 strapped to them, juggernauts, choppers, massive infantry forces, and eventually combinations of all of the above.. It gets INTENSE and this game mode is INCREDIBLY fun. Like I said, this mode alone makes MW 3 worth every penny.

So if you liked MW and MW2, definitely get this.. You will not be disappointed. Again, it is pretty much identical to MW2 in a lot of ways, but I think that's a good thing.. When Black Ops came out, the number of players seemed to dramatically decrease on MW2 to my disappointment.. Now Modern Warfare is back, and I will probably never touch Black Ops again. Also, since comparing MW to Battlefield seems to be the thing to do in reviews, in my opinion this game beats the living hell out of Battlefield.. It did win shooter of the year.. And if anything else, if you buy MW3 used, you won't have to spend extra money on an online access pass like BF 3 (which is ridiculous)

Hope this review helped!

title: Mass Effect Succeeds Again
text:
In this highly anticipated sequel, Commander Shepard continues fighting to save the galaxy, reunite with old friends, and make new ones. Mass Effect 2 does not disappoint and has been overhauled and streamlined in many ways and it is mostly a good thing.

Note: This review is written mostly from the perspective of comparing Mass Effect 1&2 (ME1 received 4 stars-4.5 stars if I could). Hope this review helps.

Pros:
-Controls are intuitive. They are easy to get used to and is context sensitive, meaning there are less keys to learn. E.g. When space is pressed, it can be used to go into cover, run, or interact with an object depending on the context.
-Combat has been streamlined. Weapons sound great and even feel like it is more powerful. Special abilities have a faster cool down period, letting you use them more frequently. Combined with smooth controls, ME2 lets you freeze, burn, throw, and pull your enemies in any combination with ease.
-It is even more cinematic than ME1 and combined with an amazing soundtrack, making it that much more immersive, dramatic, and exciting.
-There are many more characters to learn about and interact with, each with a unique personality that makes them stand out from others.
-Side quests are individually designed and has been given as much care as the main missions themselves.
-All the things that made the previous Mass Effect great are back. The dialogue wheel and decision making is back, great story telling, voice cast, drama, history, and humor are all back.
-Ability to import your saved games from the first Mass Effect.
-Without too many details, how well you play during the whole game affects the outcome of the last mission. This is simply ingenious.
-Beautiful graphics and a great price ($10-$15).

Cons:
-Minor glitches such as walking over crates, occasionally getting stuck.
-As a personal preference, there is less customization in special abilities, weapons, and armor. This is part of the streamlining process in which it may have been oversimplified and makes ME2 head towards the direction of being a straight forward shooter rather than a well balanced RPG shooter. This may please FPS (or third person shooter) enthusiasts, but less so for RPG enthusiasts (assuming you're one or the other). I, on the other hand have mixed feelings and love FPS at the same time. The lack of customizability also leads to less strategy and less trade offs.
-Some special abilities overlap. They may have different names, but generally serve the same purpose. For example, geth shields, fortifications, and barriers are all different abilities, but in terms of functionality, they all give you shields.

Note: If you play ME2 by itself, you may not care for the lack of customizability. Mass Effect 2 still stands alone as a great shooter with a great story.

Mass Effect 2 continues Bioware's impeccable story telling tradition and sets up very well for Mass Effect 3. Mass Effect 2 is very well polished, and depending on where you stand on this RPG shooter spectrum, it may very well be the perfect game. Whether you are a newcomer to the series or a Mass Effect veteran, this is not to be missed. If you played the first Mass Effect and loved the RPG elements, you won't find it here, but the story and the pace of the game will have you so engrossed that you may even forget to miss the RPG elements. Playing Mass Effect 1 before Mass Effect 2 is highly recommended.

title: Terrible software, but it can work
text:
If you must use your computer as a tv, the gamebridge will fulfill your needs. However, the software package that ships with it (InterVideo Home Theatre) is terrible, and you may need to turn to a third party solution - I wasn't even able to get InterVideo Home Theatre to run. There is no troubleshooting documentation and Adaptec's support for the product is non-existant.

I eventually ditched the InterVideo program and used Dscaler to display the video stream from the gamebridge. This worked rather well, though it requires a lot of processor power to de-interlace the video stream. Unless you have a very fast computer, you'll have to settle for a reduction in image quality or suffer many dropped frames. After picking a de-interlacing algorithm appropriate for my processor's power, there was only the occasional stutter or rendering artifact.

In summary, using the gamebridge with a laptop won't be as good as a TV, but is entirely adequate if a TV isn't available. However, if you use a monitor that is detached from your PC, try a vga converter instead.

title: Epic Fantasy RPG
text:
I've been considering getting this game for some time, but I was unsure. I bought it on sale recently, and it turned out to be one of the best games I have ever played. It is definitely worth it even at full price, and you will be hard pressed to find a game that will give you more play time and enjoyment for your money. Without completing anywhere near all of the side quests available, Origins and Origins: Awakening gave me a solid 72 hours of game play. And that is just one character! This game has great replay value, and you can easily milk hundreds of hours from it.
The game play is fantastic, and the world is huge and diverse, with very good voice acting and character writing, amazing stories, and satisfying reactions based on your choices. If you love traditional RPGs, this game is for you. But for a few bugs that are few and far between (and mostly inconsequential), this game is nearly perfect, and even though a couple of years old, it feels fresh and engaging.
The graphics are nothing overly special, but the game is relatively bugless, and feels great. You won't find yourself lamenting your purchase.
The game also has a huge amount of mods available online to customize the game play.
Overall, this is a great game, and in my top ten games of all time. If you are considering buying this, do it! I don't regret it, and neither will you.

title: Of Course You Realize This Means War
text:
Call of Duty 3 is a really fun game with extremely realistic battle sequences. The downfall is that you can only play in single player mode unless you want to do/are set up for online play.

In single player mode, you're a first person shooter soldier on the frontline in WWII France. You arrive in camp, learn how to maneuver around, shoot your weapon & throw grenades (smoke and explosive). Then you're immediately strewn into various battle.

You start out as private Nichols (American) in the first chapter, but depending on which chapter you're in, you might also find yourself playing as Doyle (British), Cole (Canadian) or Boharter (Polish).

You fight you way through intense battle chapters (there are 14 chapters). You're mostly shooting whichever weapon you happen to have picked up (mostly from dead soldiers on the ground) along your objective route (a barrage of automatics and rifles). Your objectives that guide you along are updated regularly as you complete each task throughout each chapter. And some of those tasks are brutal.

No matter which chapter you're in you are mostly using your primary weapon (a rifle or machine gun), but you'll also need to engage in some exhilarating hand to hand combat, you'll need to guide tanks, fire mortars, row boats, drive jeeps, attach and arm explosives to enemy weapons, disarm booby traps and man other stationary weapons.

To me, all of the chapters are equally difficult. So if you figure out how to unlock them all like we did, there's no reason to play them chronologically (perhaps at least for consistency chapters 1 & 14 should be played respectively first and last).

So all in all Call of Duty 3 is intensely fun, but like I said earlier, the biggest drawback to this awesome game is that multiplayer mode is only available with online play. I'm sure that online play is spectacular for advanced players, but my kids and I 1) are not advanced, and 2) we'd rather just play amongst ourselves for now. I'm no software expert, but if multiplayer capability works online, some genius should have figured out that multiplayer would be equally fun with friends/family at the same console. Hence, that is the only reason why I've deducted a star from the overall rating.

title: FROM TALIEN'S ZOMBIE SURVIVAL GUIDE JOURNAL
text:
DAY -35: Just saw an ad for Dead Rising. So jazzed! The main character kills shambling zombies in a mall with baseball bats, an umbrella, and a chainsaw. Chainsawing zombie goodness, baby! WOOHOO!

DAY 0: Just got the game. YES! Popped it in and started playing. The main character reminds me of Andrew Dice Clay from The Adventures of Ford Fairlane, only sized like a linebacker.

DAY 1: What the...the text is so small! I can't read anything!

DAY 2: Oh for the love of...Dead Rising is for HD televisions only. I can't read what Otis keeps calling me about, so I can't play the game. Sigh.

DAY 32: My brother was over for dinner and when he looked at my flat screen television in the basement, he pointed out that it's actually a high def television. Yes, I'm an idiot. Back to Dead Rising!

DAY 33: Woohoo, this rocks! So many zombies to kill! And not just zombies; the game is full of psychopaths too. I killed a clown with chainsaws, some big fat cop who looks like Kathy Kinney (from The Drew Carey Show), a pyromaniac who looks like Weird Al, and a weird raincoat/green mask-wearing cult that totally freaks me out. I'm a little behind on the main missions but the game hasn't ended yet so I figure I'm good.

DAY 34: I hate this game so much. I spent hours playing it and when I got back to the security office, the game ended and said I had missed a deadline. Information that would have been useful YESTERDAY! Maybe I'll sell it.

DAY 37: Okay, back on track. It's really upsetting that I don't have time to save all the survivors. So I of course only save the hot chicks. And this one old lady because I love my grandma (God rest her soul). A couple of times I accidentally killed one of the survivors with a sledgehammer when I was trying to kill a zombie. Mental note: people and sledgehammers don't mix.

DAY 38: OH. MY. GOD. The game just crashes at random times. It says the disc is dirty. Only the disc isn't dirty. My theory is that the game uses a huge amount of processor speed, and since I have a refurbished 360, they dialed back the processing power so the Xbox doesn't overheat anymore. Which means Dead Rising crashes it every few times. I am so selling this game, screw this!

DAY 40: It seems like there's some sort of plot to produce cattle...that led to creating zombies in a little town outside the U.S. The main psychopath decided to reveal the U.S. government's illegal experiments by unleashing the zombie plague at a mall to make a statement. It doesn't really make too much sense. Worse, there are multiple endings and I missed the chopper pick-up time on the roof of the mall. I'm going to start over from my last save point (which is few and far between). I'm starting to really hate this game.

DAY 42: I did it! Almost. Now the U.S. military is "cleaning up" the operation by killing everyone. Gee, glad I went through all the trouble to save all the hot chicks. Oh well, a few katana slices takes care of them nicely. But then there's this long battle with a tank and then some military guy who is impossible to beat. I think I'll just sell this game.

DAY 43: My wife said, "After all this complaining about the game, you BETTER finish it." So okay, I'm gonna finish it.

DAY 44: I did it! I beat the main bad guy by spinning around like a top, backslapping the bad guy with what has to be the stupidest move in gaming combat history. But I beat Dead Rising! Take that, only-one-save slot! Take that, crashing-all-the-time processor! Take that, stupid forced story-timeline! I did it! I did it! Did I mention I love this game?

I'll sell it tomorrow.

When I press the Home button I can access Systems, but I can find no option to Save my progress. If I just try to exit, it does not ask if I want to save. So the next time I log into the game, I have to start from the beginning. This has happened twice.

There is probably something simple that I'm missing, but I just don't know what it is, and I'm sick of looking for the solution. I'm not sure it's even worth trying since the games on the video are uninteresting. Maybe I'm just too spoiled by the Professor Layton series, which in contrast is very easy to understand and has a wider variety of puzzles (though I miss tapping the screen for hint coins .... the new 3DS version requires me to use a magnifying glass to find hint coins). I won't waste my time on any future versions of Doctor Lautrec.

title: Beware: No in-case pamphlet, No saves to Media..rant in progress!
text:
I am sure others have already ranted about the fact that you are only purchasing access to 97% of the disc content unless you happen to have high speed internet access. So I'll leave that gripe alone.

I would give this game concept 10 stars out of 5, except there are some execution problems (largely due to politics, why does that have to infringe on my gaming pleasure???)

The game:
I love the environments! The game play is very similar to the latest elder scrolls, but greatly improved IMHO. I like the rendering engine they used better than the one in Elder scrolls. I like the way that they implemented "mapping" as a "skill" so you can enhance your mapping abilities if
that is something that is important to you. Things like that are really thoughtful. I love the brighter than usual dungeon environments and the stylized graphics, especially how some plants glow and grow as you approach akin the Avatar movie. So, I wanted to support the fantastic work done on this game, I even bought a new copy for the PS3 (on Amazon) instead of used.

The execution: (the new politics of gaming)
With the lack of in-case pamphlet and the save game copy lockout and the online activation codes, I can't recommend buying this new. I don't have high speed internet, so I am locked out of part of the game until I can find some way to get online, update to the latest firmware (losing the "other OS" option that I currently have) and get the game registered online...that's a pain. For me, I would get all the same stuff with a used copy. The online codes are useless to me.
So unfortunately, I have to give it only 2 stars because of the glitches and politics of EA and Sony.

Problems:
I got about 46 hrs of playtime into it (13% trophies). I have experienced some oddities with the game. Some of the quests are kind of glitchy. On one, I was supposed to kill 5 of something. I killed 2 of them and happened to kill the main one (I suppose) and so it marked the quest as completed, weird. Also, I got to level 12 and could no longer purchase skills from the basic trainers, even though I only had a 1 in Mercantile, for instance. I am not certain if there are secret qualifications you have to meet to be trained or if it was glitching.

EA seems to have decided for us, that an in-case pamphlet is no longer viable, to tell you things like, what the screen icons mean and how to attack and special attack, etc. They un-thoughtfully included a "manual" on the in-game menu, if you can find it. The in-game manual, besides seeming grossly generic and incomplete (it refers to the "attack" button instead telling you its the "square", etc), is a pain to go back and forth between the game screen and then back to the soft copy of the manual to glean the information you need. When you could have just consulted a small booklet in your hand. 10 hrs into the game you really don't use it much. But at first, you might use it a lot and I think there is no excuse for it. They have no problem including plenty of other papers and codes in the case, they really aren't saving any paper. Plus, that was one of the reasons I always preferred to buy new games when possible instead of used games...I hope this is not a new trend. You need to let them know if you are dissatisfied with these new trends and commit to boycotting EA games if this is important to you.

As I mentioned, I am one of the tiny minority of 75% that DOESN'T have high speed internet. Another BIG problem I found is that EA has LOCKED OUT backing up your games onto media like memory sticks, etc!!!!!
They now try to FORCE you into buying a PS Plus membership to back up your games. This is getting ridiculous! Would like to know how this is implemented on Xbox, maybe I should have gone that route instead. I discovered this great injustice, because my install got corrupted somehow while I was sleeping and the machine was off...Hmmm.
I lost 46 hours of in-game time (about 60 hrs real-world time). I tried reloading the game and it wouldn't even run after that. I finally had to add a USER2 login to my PS3 and install Amalur under the new user before it would even install properly. Have never had this type of problem with any other PS3 game.
Also, this is the ONLY game I have seen so far that requires PS+ for backups. Once again, if you don't let EA know about your feelings regarding these changes, they will become permanent. I had heard of people boycotting EA starting last year. It didn't really mean anything to me until I became a victim of their new paradigm first-hand. It's obvious to me they have no desire to take care of their customers.

I can't say whether the game was to blame for the PS3 corruption or not.
Bottom line - Sony and EA have gotten WAY too greedy for me.

title: A new standard
text:
First of all, I'll say like everyone else, that the game is amazing. I wasn't sure I'd like it as much as I did but most of it works great.
Back when shadow of the colossus (sotc) 1st came out I remember thinking that this is what I'd like zelda games to be. And in many ways this game reminds me of sotc. Some similarities:
*The horses have a mind of their own which you guide
*Stamina limitations for climbing etc
*Gathering of fruits and animals (lizard tails in sotc)
*The Devine beasts can be liken to colossi
But while sotc was a simple game, zelda botw has taken most of those ideas and evolved into a much more elaborate game.
Weapons and shields break, don't really love it but sometimes you genuinely have to prepare your gear before certain tasks are done.
There are tons of things to gather.
Your preparation can lead to frustrating battles or comfortable victories.
Unfortunately the game is so open that the story is given in recollected memories and early in game discussions. This due to the fact that most of the game can be considered optional content.
Exploration is the heart of this game, there's always something interesting to be discovered or do, some alternative way to defeat a group of enemies... There's always something. It's great how lively this world feels.
A nice touch is how the climate affects you and the various ways in which you counter these effects. Too cool? Spicy food and warmer gear. Thunderstorm? Put away your metal gear. Its all interesting and fun, you sometimes need to explore more and discover new stuff that would make these trips more comfortable.

One note is the learning curve, because it's so open, you can find yourself feeling pretty overwhelmed by the enemies you meet up. While this is mostly due to not being prepared, you can die a lot and meet some challenges.

May edit this review when I experience more but so far the game is awesome, a must have for everyone that has a Wii U of Switch.

title: A true workout
text:
This is, hands down, my favorite exercise game for the Wii. That's not to say I always enjoy it - some of the running and lunge sets are pure torture. But it's the only program I have been able to stick with, and results started showing within a week or so. My muscles are more defined and my clothes are looser. I don't think I will be able to stick with this one program forever, but there is enough variety that I'm still going strong after 5 months.

There are a few negatives - the trainer can be annoying, the rubber band is not particularly resistant, it's irritating to keep removing and replacing the nunchuck, and once in a while, the program fails to register movements for no apparent reason.

But the good aspects far outweigh the bad. The little pointless trophies are inspiring. The weekly and monthly goals are achievable, and if you are a bit short on calories or hours during one week of a thirty-day workout, you can easily do a custom workout to meet the goal and feel good about yourself. The routines are varied enough to prevent boredom, but there aren't so many exercises that it becomes impossible to remember how to do each one. Also, the calendar rearranges itself if a workout is missed or an extra workout is done on a rest day - good for those of us with irregular schedules.

While weight loss is a good thing, my aim with this and similar programs is just to get a bit healthier. I don't enjoy the gym, and my allergy to bees makes me afraid to spend too much time outdoors in the summer. This is the first game I've found that seems effective and is easy to keep coming back to.

title: Razer Basilisk X Hyperspeed Wireless Mouse
text:
[[VIDEOID:4c2e9d2f7b0e6a0691a91cb5e893b6c]] This is a review for the Razer Basilisk X Hyperspeed Wireless Mouse.

For comparison purposes, I also use a Razer Basilisk 16,000 DPI Optical Sensor (wired) and a Logitech G502 Proteus Spectrum (wired) on a daily basis. I don’t love the wired Razer, as I’m not a fan of the scroll wheel or the design of buttons 4 and 5.

Right off, I noticed that I liked the scroll wheel on the Razer Basilisk X. It doesn’t have as much resistance as the wired version does. It’s a little clicky and has some resistance, but not so much that I revert to using my laptop’s trackpad, as I do with the wired Basilisk.

The left and right buttons are nice and clicky. The side buttons stick out a bit more on the Basilisk X than on the wired Basilisk, which I prefer.

I have small hands and found the Basilisk X comfortable to use for hours at a time.

Synapse 2 on my Mac could not find this mouse. Synapse 3 on my Windows computer did find the mouse. This mouse is only compatible with Synapse 3. On Windows, I was able to customize the different buttons.

There’s no RGB customization, as the Basilisk X is the less expensive model. I was sad to see the Razer logo doesn’t light up; yes I’m a dork who likes glowing peripherals.

The mouse can be used either wirelessly or with Bluetooth. There’s a switch on the bottom to switch between connectivity types. The Basilisk X uses one AA battery; to help with battery life, I put the switch on BT to keep from accidentally waking the mouse if I don’t have the dongle plugged in. The USB dongle can be stored inside the battery compartment. It’s very small and difficult to remove from a USB port once inserted.

In contrast to other battery powered mice I’ve used in the past, the Basilisk X’s battery compartment is on the top of the mouse. The top pops off so easily I’m worried that it will pop off while I’m using the mouse, especially during an intense moment in a game. All it takes is a little pressure in the right spot, and bam, off the battery lid goes. I really don’t like this.

I don’t have a scale, but there’s a noticeable weight difference between the wired Basilisk and the wireless Basilisk X. The Basilisk X feels very lightweight in the hand. It’s almost a bit too light for me; I notice the difference every time I switch between the mice.

title: Perfect Handheld Turn-based Strategy Game
text:
I love turn-based strategy games on the pc, but was concerned how the interface would be on a handheld. Field commander has a nice and simple user interface. The graphics and animation are nice. Speech throughout gives more personality to the characters in the story (campaign mode).

Campaign mode is a fun story driven mission oriented game. It starts off easy and gets more difficult over time.

The only problem I have with this game is the mediocre to poor AI (the reason I gave this 4 rather than 5 stars). Early on it is plain dumb (to make for easier missions) and gets a little better as you go on, but most of the difficulties later appear to be due to more difficult setups. However, campaign mode is still a great deal of fun.

The multiplayer mode bails the game's AI out. Being able to play online against other players and go up the rankings is a lot of fun and extremely challenging. You can choose different squadrons which give each player different advantages.

Overall, this is a fun game and definitely one worth buying. I can safely say that I won't sell it used either since I'll continue playing multiplayer games.

If you're lucky enough to have secured a PS5, then you know what an investment it is between the console, controllers, games, peripherals, etc.. So, having a solid way to transport your pricey gear is paramount.

This PS5 carrying case from Connyam is a great way to store & carry your system. The bag quality is on par with a heavy duty nylon laptop bag. And it's very roomy once fully expanded. Plenty of room for your unit.

There is a zipper pocket on the outside of the bag. However, there are no pockets or compartments on the interior. Instead, you are given padded fabric dividers (again, like you would find in a laptop case) that will allow you to construct compartments for your accessories, cables, etc..

There are no images or instructions included with the bag. So be sure to look at the Amazon listing for the intended layout.

I would say this bag is water resistant, but NOT waterproof. So if you had to bring it through the rain, I think you would be OK. But standing with it in the rain, I'm not sure I would want to risk it. There is also a carrying strap as well as a stitched set of handles.

So to wrap up, if you think of this bag as a heavy duty laptop case, but instead for your PS5, then you will have a very good idea of what to expect.

title: Wonderful, but not without some faults!
text:
I enjoy the occasional game and decided I wanted to get back into handheld gaming. While cell phone games do have plenty of engaging time-killing games to offer, I was missing games with some depth and story; like Zelda! So I decided to go back to my roots and get a Nintendo console (my roots are the old DMG-1).

After a shockingly small amount of research, I went and impulse purchased the New 3DS XL. If this is your first 3DS, be sure to pick up a charger as well, since, unlike just about any other device that NEEDS a charger, this system does not come with one! Taking the device out of the box, the first thing you will notice is the pristine shiny surfaces that greet you! The exterior is shiny, but don't expect it to stay pretty. It will pick up finger prints if you just look at it. Not only that, but I had scratches on it after a couple weeks of keeping it in my bag (in a pocket that was microfiber lined and all by itself).

Next thing you will notice is the weight. This device actually has some heft to it! It is only 1 or 2 tenths of an ounce lighter than the original Nintendo! I found that I did get a but of hand and wrist strain during the first could days of play. Just something to keep in mind!

Another thing you will notice is that the hinge is a bit flappy. When you open the hinge, you will hear it snap into place in two positions (and by snap, it sounds and feels like you are doing something wrong). This wouldn't be a problem since the second position is where you will want the screen opened to, but the screen moves within that position. I play a lot from a reclined or laying position, so I do notice the top screen wobbling quite a bit. I would estimate that the movement is about 5 degrees. It is enough that, if I am playing while laying down, I often find myself awkwardly positing my index fingers so they wrap around to the front of the device to keep it from moving while I am playing. I have seen video of New 3DS XLs that do not have this issue with the hinge, but most people seem to have it, and people who have contacted Nintendo say that Nintendo does not consider this to be a defect.

Even with all of the negatives I have listed, there is still so much to love about this device. The top screen is beautiful and sharp. The Super Stable 3D does great (even when you play in the dark). The console comes with a few interesting games, so even if you don't by games right away, there is definitely lots of interesting stuff to do on the device. The e-shop is great and even has some great games that you can get for relatively cheap including some old NES and Gameboy games. The controls are generally ergonomic, although I find that the D-pad can be a little uncomfortable if you are playing a game that uses that instead of letting you use the thumb pad. Streetpass and spotpass add a whole other dimension of entertainment. There are a lot of great games available for the system for almost any genre. All the old Nintendo franchises have games for the 3DS that have a terrific balance between familiar characters and new spins on gameplay that develop the story.

title: One giant step backwards for gaming-kind
text:
At first glance, Lightbringer: The Next Giant Leap for Mankind seems to be a standard hero scenario where the main character saves his crew mates and salvages the first manned mission to Mars. Unfortunately, the plot is made overly difficult by design, and the puzzles are beset with problems.

Instead of being innovative as intended, the alien language used throughout the game is actually a frustrating plot device. Since we're on the first manned mission to Mars, and presumably the first human contact with extra-terrestrials, how can the ship's computer have access to a complete database of the alien language? A much better plot development would be to discover and learn the language on the way, instead of having unexplained total access from the start.

Some of the puzzles are very simple, others exceptionally difficult, and still more ridiculously repetitive -- one puzzle in particular has to be completed nine separate times to advance the game. Many of the puzzles involve translating the alien language, and since you can't access the language translator screen and view alien writing simultaneously, you're forced to use pen and paper to complete translations from alien to English.

Even more unfortunate is a serious glitch that occurs when switching CDs, which causes the game to auto-load even though you're already running the application -- it's a bug that completely halts progression in the game. Even though a patch is available, you still need to download it in order to finish the game, a fact some gamers may not know, or, be able to do if they don't have ready access to the Internet.

The game has some interesting video sequences, but includes far too many of the character simply walking -- up and down stairs, through corridors, and down shafts, which cause the action and plot to unfold very slowly. Combined with the space-based soundtrack, the presentation is likely to put some gamers to sleep. A trip to Mars may well be a giant leap for mankind, but this adventure certainly isn't one for gamers.

title: Once you embrace the strange passage of time it becomes a fantastic story-heavy RPG.
text: Once you accept the rules of this game it is amazing! I had played the original ps1 persona a very long time ago so Persona 5's formula was very new to me. I almost quit playing this in the first few hours due to the strange setup of time passage. I would pause it and leave it paused for hours and then come back because the Story and style had sucked me in, but the game play was meeting extreme resistance. Time is not set up as hours, but slots, during school you will usually see clips of your day. Your playable time consists of mostly 2 time slots of afterschool and evening. If you socialize with someone it will take up a timeslot. In the begining going to a palace will have to be done after school and when you return you will be too tired to do any other activity that day.(Two of your male friends have a request involving a maid, take it as soon as possible and do everything you can to level up the maid as quickly as possible, she will help some with your time crunch) I gave this game 5 stars because it is a very great RPG and you just must accept that the passage of time is how this is structured and embrace it. Find ways to make the most of your time. Try to prepare enough that you can go all the way through a palace to its stopping point in one day, Stack quest for mementos as much as it will workout progression-wise, level up your confidants and social stats in the most productive ways possible. It will make you think about each choice you make and who you spend your time with and when. You will hate the cat early in this game as it will often tell you that you need to sleep and will not take no for an answer. This game is great for RPG fans, but it may be hard to just jump into a story heavy game that does have a lot of rules about time. I like to roam around a game for hours and explore, you can not do that in the same manner in this game, but it is a fantastic game in its own league.

title: The best Call of Duty game I've played yet
text:
I am a huge fan of World at War, finding the zombies, multiplayer and single player to all be excellent game modes. I was also very impressed by Call of Duty 4's single player and multiplayer, but found myself very let down by a short, offensive and unentertaining single player campaign in MW2, coupled with a buggy multiplayer experience that I gave up on within a few months of purchasing the game. (For a long list of my complaints, see the Amazon review I wrote for MW2: http://www.amazon.com/review/R2ATUPNS1NWWKR/ref=cm_cr_rdp_perm )

I was tentatively hopeful that Black Ops would provide a more enjoyable experience. I was blown away by how good this game is. First, if you view my MW2 review, every single one of the key issues/suggestions I had has been fixed/implemented in Black Ops. Beyond that, the single player is longer, more entertaining and more interesting than MW2. The multiplayer feels more like COD4 and COD:WaW than MW2, which is a very good thing in my book. However, the game does borrow many of the ideas, perks and tweaks that MW2 implemented, which results in the best COD multiplayer experience I have seen yet.

Zombies also makes a return in COD:BO, with two full fledged maps, as well as a hidden game (Dead Ops Arcade) and the classic game Zork both being accessible through a PC terminal hidden in the main menu of the game.

All said and done, a fan of the single player will find that the intel, variable difficulties and enjoyable campaign will provide over a dozen hours of entertainment. I know first hand that zombies alone can provide dozens and dozens hours of entertainment, and the multiplayer is the best online FPS experience I have had on the 360 to date. (I consider it superior to the past COD games, as well as Halo, Gears of War and Battlefield games.)

I've spent well over 250 hours on both COD4 and COD:WaW, and I highly expect to find even more enjoyment and reasons to keep playing with Call of Duty: Black Ops. While not all game types will align with everyone's tastes, I fully expect there to enough here for every fan of first person shooters to be able to find enough entertainment to justify a purchase.

title: A refreshing change.
text:
This game is great. It feels like a cross between GTA and Call of Duty with a bit of Splinter Cell for salt.

The game presents a very open world with a plethora of objectives that can be tackled in nearly any order you would like.

Nearly all vehicles are drivable, and each vehicle handles differently. Some climb mountains well, others not so much. And there are plenty of mountains to climb.

The game is beautiful and has amazing long range visuals, such that we would not have thought possible a few years ago. We took a helicopter up several thousand feet and the ground seamlessly faded away as more and more of the surrounding area became visible. Then jumping out and parachuting down was a reverse thrill of the even greater magnitude.

The missions can be done however you like. Run and gun, or snipe and scoot. Some missions will of course be more easily accomplished one way than the other but you are not penalized for using the wrong method.

The weapon and loadout system, including character customization is amazing. So many options, and it is so enjoyable to work through setting your toon up just the way you want.

On the downside, I did not find a significant difference in feel between the various weapons. While this is a little disappointing, I did not find it detracted significantly from the game.

Reminder for all racing fans there will very like be no Forza next year so all the extra content for Horizon 4 along with Motorsports 7 will be carrying us through the next year.
If I had any small complaints it that Hopefully in future iterations we can see Toyota and Mitsubishi cars also added to the games massive library of cars.

title: A good game, but not Starfox64
text:
One of the main reasons most people will buy this game is expecting a grand successor to the classic Starfox64. Unfortunately this game does not deliver that.

Don't take me wrong, this is by no means a bad game, but just like StarFox Adventures, this game is not truly the successor to the Nintendo 64 game. The game does not continue and exceed the 'original' game. The main interest for fans- Arwing battles- hasn't been improved upon at all. In fact, aside from improved graphics, they could be considered a disimprovement from the previous games. There is no real innovation in the bosses. They are much the same as bosses from previous games, their weak spots are more evident than ever, and require nothing but mindless blasting to defeat. Powerups such as bombs and hyper lasers have been almost eradicated in this game and are rarely used. Flying an Arwing is still fun, but emphasis in this game was shifted elsewhere.

Instead of concentrating on great Space Battles, a large portion of the game is spent on foot with a blaster. While this part of gameplay isn't poorly done, it's somewhat boring when all you really want is to fly your ship. The game creators did a decent job at creating a balance of power between the arwing, landmaster and pilot, but ultimately we aren't really interested.

The format of the game has also taken a change. Whereas Starfox64 let you choose your root through the Lylat System (greatly increasing replay value in my opinion) Assault only has one course of action and focuses on a linear storyline. Starfox Assault is significantly longer than Starfox64 and so replay is mostly limited to individual levels instead of replaying the entire game to achieve a higher score.

Still, replaying levels will allow you to earn awards and unlock special features for multiplayer. Multiplayer mode is fast-paced fun and can provide hours of great gameplay.

Despite my criticism, StarFox Assault is still a great game, whether you're a fan or new to the Starfox series. Just don't expect it to be the great replacement for Starfox64. For that, I think StarFox Command for the DS might turn out to be a better pick, or you could just wait a few years for something new to come out on the Wii.

title: RPG for PC goes console
text:
I have to agree with a couple of the other reviews that are already up: this game's a disappointment, especially after such a terrific lead-in as "Dragon Age: Origins".

I've been playing RPGs since before the first game in the Ultima series; that was decades ago. RPGs were developed back in the days when consoles didn't exist. They were designed around PCs. One of the main reasons I never switched to Macs was that there was no gaming software developed for them to speak of. If you were a gamer, you played on a PC.

And I have to acknowledge that maybe the younger generation which grew up with Playstations and Xboxes and all that may really like this game. But I'm an old hand and a traditionalist when it comes to gaming.

On the upside, the visuals and graphics in this game are absolutely phenomenal. No question.

But this time around, they've managed to take the "role" out of "role-playing".

Most notably, you no longer get to choose your character's dialogue. That ability alone kills the immersiveness of the game. Previously, as you chose what your character was going to say a real conversation could (or may not) develop, depending on your choices. Instead, we now have a "dialogue wheel" which allows you to choose (generally) one of three tenors for your statement, sincere/conciliatory, joking, or hostile. So, you click on one and then your character speaks whatever he's going to say. I was often very surprised by what popped out of his mouth, and often found myself thinking that I certainly wouldn't have chosen that option if I knew what was actually going to be said.

Obviously, this wheel severely limits the range of conversational options, and the player's actual engagement in what's going on.

Combat is fast. And I mean FAST. There's no longer any real strategy involved. It's pretty much just hack-and-slash. Again, obviously the console approach, not traditional PC RPG. There's no longer any real ability to set up a strategy in your battles as you could in the previous game. In Origins, I was a master at ambushing and luring opponents into traps. Well... that's not really much of an option anymore. Now it's "I see you!", and the furball's on. Boring.

Too bad. After Origins I had high hopes for the re-emergence of the traditional RPG for PCs. Clearly, the developers - at least, in this case, Bio-Ware - have made the decision to design around the console players and turn the game into a button-mashing experience. Naturally, that's their decision to make, and I guess if that's where the money is in their market, maybe I'd do the same thing, too.

But the metaphor that comes to mind is that if you were looking to read a good novel, in this case you'd be buying a comic book.
